**Status on 2026-11-17:** **PROCEED WITH A CONDITIONAL LAUNCH BLOCKER.** The completed novel and working print/ebook packages exist and were locally inspected. They have **not** been independently human-edited, legally cleared for every platform, assigned an ISBN, approved by any store, physically proofed, or observed selling. This is **one project for one book**. It is **not** an instruction to write another novel, spawn unrelated book niches, republish duplicates, create accounts, use payment credentials, or commit money. External effects remain **not started**.

The only already-registered and directly relevant source IDs found were `V2-01` (Payhip free-plan pricing) and `V2-28` (Payhip email consent); both are present in the frontmatter. The official KDP, ISBN Canada, Draft2Digital, Kobo, Apple, Google, IngramSpark, B&N, etc. URLs cited below are **not** registered in the repository's `SOURCE_REGISTER.json`, so do **not** claim that the project has a complete source-register record or that `build_browser.py --check` passed. ## 1. Project decision, exact idea and fidelity contract

**Owner's original request (verbatim):** “create project just for the book and publishing it on every website it can”. **Budget from the owner-supplied universal project prompt:** `BUDGET_CEILING_CAD: 100`. The prompt's generic `PROJECT_IDEA` edit field was empty; this actual conversation request supplies the idea and overrides that placeholder. The budget is a planning cap, **not** spending permission.

**Finished result:** An adult English-language dark-comedy/crime-thriller novel called **FREE CANDY**, credited to **Chad Bradson**, available to purchase and actually receive as a quality-controlled EPUB on all *eligible, nonduplicated* meaningful ebook channels and as a verified 6×9-inch cream-paper matte paperback on technically/legally eligible print channels, with consistent cover, metadata, rights disclosures, sample, royalty tracking, and a no-cost-first discovery plan. “On every website” means maximize **appropriate reach**, not upload to inappropriate services, clone listings, evade an AI policy or use exclusive channels in conflict with wide distribution.

**Must preserve:**
- The *existing* completed **27-chapter** novel, its first-person Arthur Bell voice, dry/procedural dark humour, heightened but emotionally serious consequences, chronology, titles, character arcs and established ending. Preserve human choices already made in the story; **do not restart the manuscript**.
- Arthur, a former Danton Home & Garden returns worker, begins with an ill-conceived white van marked **FREE CANDY**, wanting to be useful. His failure to respect “no” makes him abduct **Maya Price, Benji Cole, Poppy Serrano** despite believing he is helping. Arthur is flawed and responsible, even though his intentions were initially charitable.
- Maya is the protective older child who must eventually be able to let adults protect the others. Benji's **Mega Sour Satellites** and foot/sweatshirt injuries matter. Poppy's **Strawberry Clouds**, yellow raincoat, missing broken-tailed dinosaur and parents Rafael/Inez matter. Objects evolve into symbols of choice and home, not redemption tokens.
- Calder Confectionery is a **real candy factory/legitimate family attraction**; its criminal owner Gideon March/Hawthorn **misuses collected family information** for child trafficking. **Calder's tour/factory is NOT the destination/holding place for kidnapped children**; the secluded woodland property is. Do not supply real-life criminal operational instructions.
- Russell Venn's woodland encounter, genuine police (Ortiz, Hurst, Chen, Quinn), falsely uniformed transfer, captive Nell Corbett/Idris Shaw, crew Pike/Lennie/Dean, blackmail into transporting children, second public kidnapping, return to the cabin, Arthur's absurd failed paperwork/safety-inspection plans accidentally aiding rescue, 911/YouTube/Roblox events, the rescue through others' competent actions and the final tragic reversal: children safely reunited before Arthur dies in March's grotesque explosion.
- Owner-approved publishing choices: visible author **Chad Bradson** (pen name), **FREE CANDY** in capitals, no subtitle/tagline on cover, no dedication, no acknowledgments, no author bio, cinematic van at dusk by blurred playground, dark vignette, **simple white title/author typography** (NOT exaggerated blood-dripping type), 6×9 black-and-white interior, cream paper, matte paperback cover, wide distribution, approximately 248 physical pages as current proof baseline. The current standalone EPUB and print files are source assets, **not proof of platform acceptance**.

**Flexible:** Human editorial corrections, accessibility and layout fixes, platform-specific image compression, print cover conversion to each printer template, listing copy, selected distributors, regional price hypotheses, sample/excerpt length, optional later hardcover/audiobook **only after** first formats succeed. A human editor may legitimately increase print pages if 248-page typography is uncomfortably small; never sacrifice readability merely for a page-count promise.

**Non-goals:** New sequel; unrelated games/products; unauthorized copycat cover; children's-book positioning; fabricated reviews/awards; writing under a false human-only declaration; fake ISBN, barcode, seller identity or receipts; buying traffic; publishing to incompatible or duplicate channels; preemptively enrolling in Kindle Unlimited/KDP Select; automatic physical proofs/orders or account registration.

**Audience/positioning:** Adults interested in absurdist crime fiction, morally compromised unreliable narrators, escalating failures, dark situational comedy, unsettling thrillers and endings with real consequences. NOT a family novel or children's candy-themed entertainment. Content advisory: child abduction, trafficking, coercion, gun violence, serious injury, death. The comedic target is Arthur's broken logic, **not** the children's suffering. Do not frame the hero as a competent kidnapper or promise a happy resolution.

**Quality and viability verdict:** Strong, memorable thematic hook and finished assets make a modest, low-cost release experiment **plausible**, **not commercially validated**. Against it: extensive AI-generated prose (serious distribution/rights gate), a title that may not be unique, difficult tonal balance, dense 248-page composition for ~127k words, low existing audience and genre/cover misclassification risk. Do not invent demand, sales or success probability.

## 3. Reader, offer, competition and business constraints

**Reader job-to-be-done:** Buy a complete, professionally presented adult darkly comic thriller that begins with an absurd but recognizable bad idea and becomes morally serious. Hook: a meticulous unemployed man believes he can help children with a free-candy van; the criminal organization he accidentally disrupts mistakes his spectacular ineptitude for expertise. Differentiator: procedural unreliable narrator, candy as symbolic unwanted gift, the same failed thinking accidentally enabling others to rescue themselves, and deceptive emotional closure before a tragic ending.

**Demand evidence vs. conjecture:** Genre-adjacent published titles and review conversations demonstrate an existing taste for satire with crime, **not** paid demand for this novel. Examples for positioning only: *A Particularly Nasty Case* (Adam Kay, documented listing at https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/226924089-a-particularly-nasty-case), *I Might Be in Trouble* (Daniel Aleman, profiled at https://www.novelsuspects.com/book-list/black-humor-6-mystery-thriller-where-satire-meets-comedy/), and *Psycho Samaritan* (Leon A.C. Qualls, https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/46204904-psycho-samaritan). These are **comparable audience signals only**, not creative templates, bestseller forecasts, or a claim that this book has the same reader base. No reliable seller conversion, keyword volume or sales figures observed.

**Competing options:** Traditionally edited dark-comedy thrillers, free serialized fiction, Kindle Unlimited exclusives, cheap self-published ebooks, library loans, online shorts and AI-generated fiction. Marketing must lead with a real reader experience, professional editing, truthful warnings and sample—not “AI can write it quickly.” No promise of realistic police procedure, child-safe reading or true crime reporting; it is fiction.

**Important refusal condition:** If a specific store's actual AI/rights policy excludes this work, **do not recategorize, conceal AI generation, misdeclare human authorship, or submit through an aggregator as an evasion**. Mark that destination blocked and prioritize lawful alternatives and substantive human redrafting where genuinely sufficient under the store policy.

## 5. Finished-book specification and editorial production bible

### 5.1 Source of truth and edition contract

- **Canon** is one English-language 27-chapter novel credited **Chad Bradson**, title **FREE CANDY**. Current print has 248 pages because of tight type/layout; EPUB has ~127k words. Verify cover title, metadata, copyright line and store descriptions match exactly; pen name need not equal private legal payee name.
- **Primary edition A:** reflowable, accessible EPUB 3 with 27 chapter documents, one real navigation TOC, correct `en-CA` (or set region-appropriate language only if actual text changed), proper heading hierarchy, embedded front cover, valid metadata, no fixed-print pagination masquerading as ebook pages. Owner must hold rights for every included image/font; no font-file redistribution.
- **Primary edition B:** 6×9 black-and-white cream-paper matte paperback; body PDF at 6×9 with no extra cover inserted; separate full-wrap cover with bleed/spine/barcode region, matching printer-calculated spine. Any revised page count requires rebuild of cover and TOC. Existing 248 pages are the **baseline**, not an immutable target if proof is uncomfortable.
- **Secondary:** 249-page combined PDF is a *review copy*, not the KDP paperback upload. Sample excerpt (free, separately produced by authorized workflow later), optional accessible non-DRM EPUB sold directly, alternate printer covers. Do not default to PDF as the ebook offered by Kindle/Apple/Kobo.
- **Back matter:** no dedication, acknowledgments, or author bio (owner explicitly declined). Copyright/title pages and content advisory are retained; exact copyright statement and rights claim require legal/content review before publication. Never invent an ISBN or false copyright-registration status. A closing `THE END` is part of the actual narrative, not a separate afterword.

### 5.2 Character, theme and prose constraints for the required revision

**Narrator:** Arthur Bell, first person, returns/inventory procedural brain, genuinely wants to be useful, stubbornly confuses process with consent; dry observations and a habit of making increasingly absurd but superficially orderly plans. His reliability must remain imperfect but the authorial treatment of harmed children must not be dismissive. His growth consists of accepting consequences and ceasing to demand thanks/forgiveness, **not** suddenly becoming a mastermind.

**Three children:** Maya must remain active, angry, protective and finally relieved of the job of guarding everyone; Benji retains his tart humour and sour-candy preference, injury, and desire for his mother; Poppy holds on to the broken-tailed dinosaur and Strawberry Clouds as memories of freely chosen childhood treats. Maya's wish to be believed is not reduced to Arthur's redemption device. All three are reunited with parents **before** the final chapter's deadly reversal.

**Parents and helpers:** Rafael/Inez Serrano rescue Poppy; Benji and Maya reunite with their mothers; Mrs. Wren, Nadia Shah, Dev Malik, Owen Mercer, Chen/Hurst/Quinn repeatedly offer real help. Nell and Idris produce independent evidence; Lennie and Dean cooperation does not erase their complicity; Pike's loyalty and March's exploitation remain distinct. No magical knowledge in first-person scenes while Arthur is unconscious.

**Location distinction:** Calder factory in **Grayling** is a legitimate family attraction, normal employees and visitors, and the source of private family details abused by criminals. **Never** describe it as the site where Hawthorn routinely receives/kidnaps children. **Woodland house/cabin** is a separate holding location. The second white van has passenger seats and three adult accomplices; Arthur's original van was a cargo vehicle and remains in genuine police evidence. First gun confiscated by police; second acquired from the caretaker during inspection. All genuine named officers remain genuine; only the later transport crew impersonate police.

- If D2D can't lawfully accept manuscript, examine **StreetLib's ebook** policy and metadata options and choose only unused outlets; do not use it to sneak a prohibited book into a retailer that directly refused it. **Do not launch StreetLib print from Canadian account** given official ineligibility.
- **Avoid PublishDrive paid plan** unless owner specifically prefers it and updated ROI covers subscription. Its free 3-store ebook route duplicates Apple/B&N/Kobo direct and yields little incremental reach; if selected, move ownership from direct first and document the change.
- **Print wholesale:** once appropriate ISBN and costs are confirmed, produce a fresh IngramSpark-specific cover, set printing, retailer wholesale discount and **nonreturnability default until owner explicitly chooses otherwise**. Do not enable KDP Expanded Distribution for the same print title. Wait for actual distributor/retailer acceptance; note that bookstores order on demand at their discretion. Alternative Lulu Global only in place of—not concurrent with—IngramSpark; its review fee and other costs require owner approval.
- **Lulu bookstore only/Bookvault direct:** optional secondary physical channels with distinct storefront/fulfillment advantage. Don't launch them automatically for a book without a direct-order audience. If using B&N Press print as another direct retailer route, verify unique ISBN rules and no duplicate B&N wholesaler feed.

**Wave 3: marketing and tracking after verified live**: Author hub with direct current links → adult-appropriate social/book-community posts → excerpt/sample → optional library-interest submission (no actual book orders falsely implied) → weekly/30-day royalty and refund reconciliation → price/description/cover iteration only on observed data and with owner signoff. No fake preorders, giveaway claims or manufactured reviews.

**Country and tax safeguards:** The user operates from Canada, but **seller tax residency, business registration, beneficial payee and banking must be provided privately by owner**; do not put them in this public Markdown. Each service may issue U.S. tax questionnaire or charge/recollect tax; the local project has no authority to choose treaties, sign tax declarations or interpret legal obligations as advice. For earnings display, keep original settlement currency (USD, CAD, EUR etc.), transaction date and platform fee; convert only using a recorded date/rate/source in private reporting. The public record must never contain tax IDs, email inboxes, addresses or payment keys.

**ISBN / edition discipline:** One ISBN for a paperback edition per format/identifying publication properties; hardcover needs separate ISBN. An ebook may require a different ISBN in some distribution systems, while KDP Kindle doesn't. **No arbitrary fake ISBN**. If an ISBN assigned at a distributor cannot be ported, do not try to use it at the competing print distributor. Changing a cover's art alone ordinarily isn't a wholly new edition, but changes to imprint/format/rights/ISBN may require re-registration. Confirm printer account rules rather than inferring from a file name. The same book's `FREE CANDY` title may coincide with other works; do not assume trademark clearance or exclusive title rights.

**Rollback/withdrawal / correction:** Immediately log any mistaken upload with affected platform, version, submitted files, status and confirmation ID. If submission is **uncertain**, query status before retrying; never duplicate. Withdraw/unpublish via the **same account/aggregator owner**; direct/wholesale feeds and third-party cached listings may take weeks to update. Do not promise instant removal from libraries or third-party sellers. Preserve all actual customer support/revision communications in authorized private workspace. Correct sensitive erroneous files and metadata with a controlled edition change and update downstream caches only after owner approves. If a complaint or DMCA/rights claim arrives, halt promotions and request legitimate review rather than automatically fighting it.

## 12. Post-launch operating and maintenance playbook

**Weekly for first month (once actually live):** reopen each listing URL; check descriptions, adult metadata, cover thumbnail/author, prices, file samples, reported buyers and refunds; note distribution delays. Reconcile payout balances vs transaction reports and fees. Record responses to genuine customer questions without sharing buyer details publicly. Fix technical corruption without rewriting user-visible prose by stealth. Monitor price parity where stores require it; do not assume all regional prices must be identical after tax/FX.

**Monthly:** consolidate channels into one private ledger keyed `platform + edition + product ID + period + currency`, track gross purchases separately from units licensed/reads and from net operating contribution. Note promotion sources and attributable time. Review returns/chargebacks and actual paper cost. If a listing is stuck or rejected, capture exact error, fix/review compliance, and avoid repeated prohibited resubmission. Assess whether the first $0 marketing lane is generating qualified traffic; broaden only when useful. Budget ceiling review is **not** an automatic reset.

**Support and fixes:** Provide a stable public support address or store-native contact under the pen name once approved; owner controls access. Standard response should acknowledge reported EPUB/PDF/print defect, identify platform/device/edition version, offer a corrected file or seller-authorized refund as required, and log effect privately. No promise of unlimited free replacements or direct off-platform payments without policy review. For serious sensitive-content complaints, review content advisory and actual scene/marketing mismatch. For child-safety concerns, do not imply real reports or real victims existed: the novel is fiction.

**Maintenance releases:**
- `1.0.x` = typos, accessibility metadata, formatting and approved corrections with no major plot change.
- `1.1.x` = owner-approved substantive changes, cover/reader material updates, likely store metadata/ISBN policy review.
- `2.0.0` = new significant edition (e.g. material rewrite, print format): check need for new ISBN, old copies, linked reviews and preserved catalog history.
- Keep all 27 chapter titles and final events unless owner expressly authorizes a new edition. Never silently change published edition text to satisfy one reader's review.

**Follow-on opportunities (explicitly not current projects):** Separate audiobook if actual human narration is produced/licensed and verified; hardcover if buyers request it and print costs work; translations only with qualified review/rights and separate edition ISBNs, each as a child task/SKU within BOOK-001 unless truly a new business. Do not call a planned audiobook an available store listing.

## 13. Risks, adversarial review and open owner decisions

| Risk / argument against launch | Practical mitigation without changing the book's identity | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| **AI-generated text and artwork** face D2D/Kobo/ISBN restrictions and uncertain copyright scope | Document exact AI/human contributions, seek actual substantial human creative edit and legal review, disclose on KDP/other platforms, obtain ISBN Canada written guidance instead of signing a false human-only declaration. | **Hard blocker for restricted routes** |
| Public copyright page currently shows `© 2026 Chad Bradson` | A pen name is permitted for public branding, but copyright notice is not evidence of rights and platform payee still needs private legal details. Owner/counsel decides final wording/rights support. | Owner signoff required |
| 248 printed pages from ~127k words may look dense | Actual print proof/readability test; permit page count to rise, automatically regenerate spine/TOC and new files; do not shrink below comfortable legibility. | Preprint gate |
| Full wrap may fail other printer's bleed/spine/barcode | Use each publisher's generated template and ISBN; don't send KDP PDF as universal wrap. | Print channel-specific gate |
| Violent subject involving children may be miscategorized or rejected | Adult fiction classification and honest advisory, respectful promotional copy; no false guarantee of acceptance. | All stores review |
| Potential title collision `FREE CANDY`, cover similarity to existing book | Search exact title/pen name/cover before uploading; no assumed trademark; distinguish through description/author/cover. | Verify |
| Readers reject Arthur as sympathizable or final abrupt explosion | Editing/beta-style internal craft audit, foreshadow through theme without spoiling twist, ensure children's recovery isn't erased. Marketing should signal black comedy/thriller, not playful children's gift. | Human judgment gate |
| All-store publication duplicates and incompatible rights | One distributor owner per retailer and ISBN; KDP Select OFF; disable Expanded Distribution if Ingram wholesale. | System invariant |
| Print returns or paid aggregators exceed CAD100 | Default nonreturnable/zero subscriptions; receive actual fee quotes before proposing spend, cap total owner exposure, pause blocked channels. | Budget gate |
| Low organic reach / no verified paid demand | Strong excerpt, targeted discoverability, measured experiments, stop optimizing obscure stores until the main listing is convincing. | Commercially unvalidated |
| Existing Payhip store publicly associated with a different identity | Owner must approve new pen-name-branded storefront or skip; do not leak legal real name or connect brands without permission. | Privacy gate |
| User files exist only in ChatGPT workspace, not Codex Windows checkout | Owner-authorized import with hashes to a private folder; public project record links asset roles, not full paid files. | Transfer gate |
| Agent publishing/charging before permission | Write-only local previews until explicit, scoped owner approval for each account action, cost and publication. Preserve state and uncertain effects. | Hard safety gate |

**Open decisions requiring real human answers or an actual third party (not a reason to stall local planning):**

1. Who legally owns the textual and cover rights, and what genuine human expressive editing has been done? The public pen name is already chosen as **Chad Bradson**, but account legal identity is private.

4. Does owner approve reuse of the existing differently branded direct-sales account, or is a distinct pen-name shop preferred?
5. Which platform account terms, payout/banking/tax terms and AI fields actually apply at submission? A partner's public help page is not proof of approval for the account.
6. Does owner authorize any real paid print proof, ISBN acquisition or book marketer within CAD100? **Currently: no spend authorized.**

None of these requires an arbitrary questionnaire or market interview to **start** the local project. An actual rights affirmation, professional edit, platform account authorization and purchases are naturally human-controlled release gates.

## Execution persistence for this project



When the owner asks you to work on this project, continue autonomously through all remaining authorized tasks possible with available access and resources. Do not stop merely because a few minutes passed, after one task, a plan, or a progress update. Continue implementation, appropriate verification, evidence recording, and the next actionable task until the requested work is finished or no further authorized work can be performed. Give progress updates without ending longer work. If authorization, access, payment, another person, or external state blocks an action, complete independent authorized work first, then checkpoint and report the precise blocker and next action. Preserve completed progress, financial evidence, and uncertain external effects; respect existing scope, budget, permissions, and safety controls. Never claim unverified completion.



# Historical Save Regression Lab — Complete Business and Implementation Plan



## 1. Executive decision and current status



**Decision: retain as a high-priority, unvalidated technical product candidate.** Make a **Unity editor-only package** that runs historical save fixtures through the customer's *real* load/migration entry point and validates meaningful restored game state. The initial sellable outcome is a reproducible failing assertion such as "the file loaded successfully, but the upgraded player lost a unique item." Its marketable differentiator must be *speed of integration and meaningful diagnostics*, not generic serialization or a new save system.



- **Exact buyer:** independent Unity studios maintaining released save-compatible games; secondarily teams developing long-lived simulation/RPG projects and maintainers of save middleware.

- **Buyer trigger:** an update changes save schema or runtime restoration; regression testing of old versions is difficult and expensive to maintain.

- **Chosen earliest channel:** Unity Asset Store *if accepted*; direct checkout is a fallback, not proof of audience. No seller account is assumed.

- **First contribution target:** a few CAD69-equivalent paid units per month could contribute to the portfolio's CAD150/month milestone; see the transparent scenario math in §8.

- **Scope:** Unity-only initial edition; other engines are independently researched extensions. This **does not** authorize full multi-engine implementation or a universal save parser.

- **Reality check:** no paid customers, interviews, beta trials, engine tests, files from customers, or release have been verified. The project is `planned` and `unvalidated`, not "ready to sell".

- **Why continue rather than cancel today?** A concrete technical test can verify the differentiator locally without human interviews, paid tooling or proprietary games. **Kill** the product if a small set of well-written Unity Test Framework tests offers equivalent results with less setup.



## 2. Repository baseline, duplication and reuse



Verified public repository: `Hi62384/Proj`, `main` at `6f2a420e9a1d7d5b44ec1759918e737059a6772e`, reviewed 2026-11-15. Canonical location is `business_portfolio/niches/digital-products/game-development-marketplaces/projects/gdm-001-historical-save-regression-lab/project.md`, niche ID `N-gdm-20261115`, project ID `GDM-001`. The other active game-development records are `GDM-002` (passenger transport) and `GDM-003` (packaging/dependencies): different jobs-to-be-done, not duplicates. Older portfolios/research are preserved in `business_portfolio/archive/2026-11-15-legacy/`, `archive/2026-11-15-taxonomy-view-v1/` and `opportunity_library/`. This file revises GDM-001; **do not create a new project ID**, overwrite an archive or reset historical work.



**Reuse:** the repository's project browser, test/checkpoint system, source register, marketing research, and prior `results/GDM-001/` research files (if present). The historical Unity discovery interview guide is retained for continuity but **is not** a development dependency. No existing production save-test library for this project was observed in the published repository records; Codex must inspect the **current local checkout** before creating a source tree.



**Distinctness screening (not new business ideas):** generic save engines and migration pipelines are adjacent substitutes; Unreal already has a dedicated historical-save test product. The GDM-001 opportunity only survives if a Unity-specific integration/reporting gap is real. Do not repackage a free tester or create a separate "save migrator" as another active project.



## 3. Opportunity discovery and selection record



The owner's earlier marketplace workbook evaluated **33 directions** and retained six candidates. This revision re-evaluates *this existing selected family*, not a fresh 15–30-idea opportunity generation run. Nearby options and decisions:



| Adjacent direction | Decision | Specific reason |

|---|---|---|

| Sell a general JSON/binary save framework | Reject | Numerous free and paid options; easy to build a basic version. |

## 4. Buyer, buying trigger, and reasons to decline



Buyer A maintains an RPG with old player characters/inventory; Buyer B maintains a survival or simulation title with evolving world-state flags. ```csharp

public interface IHistoricalLoadAdapter

{

    string AdapterId { get; }

    Task<ObservedState> CaptureStateAsync(CancellationToken cancellation);

## 11. Data contracts, deterministic algorithms and failure recovery



**Proposed fixture manifest (version 1):**



```json

{

  "schema_version": 1,

  "suite_id": "example-v1-to-v3",

  "fixtures": [{

    "fixture_id": "player-before-inventory-refactor",

    "source_game_version": "1.0.0",

    "target_game_version": "3.0.0",

    "file": "fixtures/player-v1.save",

    "sha256": "REPLACE_WITH_REAL_64_HEX_SHA256",

    "timeout_seconds": 30,

    "assertions": [

      {"path": "inventory.unique.shield_01", "type": "boolean", "equals": true},

      {"path": "quests.main.completed", "type": "boolean", "equals": false},

      {"path": "player.hp", "type": "number", "equals": 75, "tolerance": 0}

    ]

  }]

}

```



`sha256` is an *illustrative placeholder*, not a fabricated fixture fingerprint. Before executing, verify actual fixture hash, schema, and relative path beneath an allowlisted root. Reject absolute/traversal/symlink escapes. Sandbox path must be distinct and disposable; cleanup must respect an opt-in debug-retain mode. Nested property paths use a documented escaped-dot grammar; explicit strict type comparison prevents strings passing as numbers. Numeric tolerance is only applied to declared numeric paths; NaN/Infinity are invalid for deterministic manifests. Each result includes fixture and game versions, adapter identity, source hash, expected/observed values **redacted by default**, repro command, and one of `pass`, `regression`, `invalid_fixture`, `unsupported`, `timeout`, `adapter_error`.



**Core algorithm:**



```text

for fixture in suite.sorted_by_stable_id:

    validate_manifest_and_hash(fixture) -> reject invalid before touching game

    sandbox = fresh_private_copy(fixture)

    adapter.ResetAsync(); await adapter.RestoreAsync(sandbox.path, timeout)

    observed = await adapter.CaptureStateAsync()

    normalized = canonicalize(observed, approved_schema, deterministic_sorting)

    for assertion in fixture.assertions:

        if path_absent/type_mismatch: emit explicit regression-or-adapter-error

        else compare typed value with declared numeric tolerance

    emit structured result with stable diagnostic code and redacted diff

    assert original fixture SHA256 unchanged; cleanup sandbox

return report; fail CI when any regression/adapter_error/timeout/invalid_fixture exists

```



**Performance / privacy:** initial QA target ≤25 original synthetic fixtures and up to 1,000 explicit assertions per suite without unsupported memory growth; *measure* on a specified Windows machine/Unity version before claiming capacity. Avoid fixture-content logs by default, verify no network egress and no filesystem write outside sandbox and approved report folder. Do not use `Application.persistentDataPath` blindly—confirm the selected game's loader can be redirected to a disposable profile without modifying real user saves.



**Failure recovery:** crash mid-test leaves source untouched; incomplete report explicitly says aborted; next run makes a new sandbox. Unexpected external I/O requests are refused or reported unsupported. Multiple suite runs must not race on the same game profile; serialize until isolation is proven.

See `results/GDM-001/isolation-and-baseline-review-2026-11-18.md`.





### 2026-11-18 descendant timeout and hard-link canaries



A restricted synthetic Unity player started a long-lived child that reported AppContainer token and job membership. The supervisor observed the child alive at the deadline, terminated the job, observed that child exit and zero active associated processes, and deleted the temporary profile. Separately, a hard link inside each temporary player profile pointed to a disposable outside file: the unrestricted control changed its target, while the restricted attempt raised `UnauthorizedAccessException` and its target stayed unchanged. These are bounded tests, not proof against all process-creation methods, links, inherited handles or hostile reports. See `results/GDM-001/isolation-and-baseline-review-2026-11-18.md`.





### 2026-11-18 junction and inherited-handle canaries



A disposable directory junction inside each temporary player location pointed to a synthetic outside file. The unrestricted control changed its target; the AppContainer player received `UnauthorizedAccessException` and left its target unchanged. Junctions were removed before profile cleanup. Separately, an explicitly allowlisted writable file handle was deliberately inherited by a no-capability AppContainer process, which wrote through that handle successfully. This demonstrates why inherited handles must be controlled; it does not demonstrate that the current standalone supervisor leaks one. Additional path, handle and report-integrity tests remain necessary. See `results/GDM-001/isolation-and-baseline-review-2026-11-18.md`.





### 2026-11-18 handle and report-integrity tests



The restricted standalone player could write to a deliberately allowlisted inherited handle, but with the supervisor's no-inheritance setting the identical handle did not identify the target and the target remained empty. A separate deliberately dishonest restricted player wrote a start marker and `pass` result without invoking restoration, and exited 0; the current supervisor accepted the worker-produced JSON. Thus isolation does not authenticate gameplay observations or prevent a malicious worker from forging its own report. This is a release-blocking trust-model gap, not evidence that all isolation architectures fail. See `results/GDM-001/isolation-and-baseline-review-2026-11-18.md`.





### 2026-11-18 loader and report-contract experiment



A restricted standalone synthetic Unity player used a namespace-wrapped copy of the existing sample game loader with v1, v2 and v3 fixtures. All three passing cases exited 0; injected shield and quest faults exited 1 with the expected paths. A separate unrestricted v1 control also passed. Restricted runs reported AppContainer tokens, unchanged copied fixtures, no outside canary, zero active job processes, and successful temporary-profile deletion. The parent-side experimental contract checks pinned fixture hashes, report structure and exit consistency, and defaults to an untrusted-worker result. The earlier fabricated pass is still accepted if a caller explicitly asserts worker trust, demonstrating that these checks do not authenticate gameplay. This remains synthetic, Windows-specific experimental work; the native comparison and production isolation and trust model remain open. Next: assess an equivalent native comparison and define the trusted integration boundary. See `results/GDM-001/isolation-and-baseline-review-2026-11-18.md`.





### 2026-11-18 trusted integration and separate Unity CI comparison



Documented the proposed trust boundary: a reviewed game, adapter, build, assertions, supervisor and host must be trusted; confinement and report validation cannot authenticate hostile in-process claims. Added a repeatable test using the actual previously forged report; it is untrusted by default but structurally passes when worker trust is asserted. Six report-contract tests passed. In separate Unity 6000.6.9f1 runs, native and prototype integrations each passed all three synthetic save versions; a paired suite passed six cases with two intentional CI tests skipped. Four separately invoked negative CI runs (native and prototype for shield and quest) each exited 2 and reported the expected path. This is an equivalent synthetic behavior comparison, not independent setup or maintenance evidence, real-game validation, production isolation, or proof of advantage. Next: assess actual-game integration and independent effort; defer release pending those gates. See the isolation review and native comparison scorecard.





### 2026-11-18 real-game candidate and independent study preparation



The owner confirmed no Unity game or independent developer is available. Cloned the public MIT-licensed NightRealm repository for local research at commit `9fd092d0b235c725cf281e1da5d97da51e5ccd31`. Static review found a multi-file save path under Unity persistent data, gameplay load/save hooks and a source-level candidate XP-save defect; the game has not been run, the defect is unverified, and historical saves have not been found. The current one-file in-Editor prototype is not safely contained for this game. Recorded the trust, disposable environment and multi-file prerequisites plus a prospective independent setup and maintenance protocol in `results/GDM-001/real-game-integration-study-2026-11-18.md`. Independent measurement is blocked by the absence of an independent developer; no outreach or payment is authorized. No game data or upstream repository was changed. Next: establish contained execution with a scratch save root and then test the pinned candidate; obtain an independent developer for the benchmark.



### 2026-11-18 multi-file staging preparation

Added an experimental Python staging helper for multiple named SHA-256-pinned synthetic files and two passing tests for copy isolation, cleanup and rejection of invalid names or hashes. This does not redirect NightRealm, enforce process isolation, address all filesystem races or reparse points, or establish real-game restoration. Next: establish a contained game environment and redirect its complete save root before attempting the pinned game.


### 2026-11-18 contained NightRealm Editor startup probe

A supervisor copied the pinned game into a unique no-capability Windows AppContainer profile and patched only the disposable copy to point its save root at a new folder in that profile. An opt-in Editor probe was prepared to round-trip synthetic GameStatus and PlayerLevel files through the game's SaveLoadHandler, but the actual restricted Unity 6000.6.9f1 Editor exited 1 before the probe ran. Its log reported a Package Manager IPC connection failure. AppContainer token was confirmed; there were no created save files, job accounting reached zero active processes, and the temporary profile was deleted. The original checkout stayed unchanged. Thus neither the save redirection nor actual gameplay restore was runtime-verified. See `results/GDM-001/real-game-integration-study-2026-11-18.md` and `experiments/nightrealm-appcontainer-observation.json`. Next: investigate an appropriately contained build/player route or a safe Unity-compatible boundary without weakening ACLs or exposing real saves; an independent developer remains unavailable.


### 2026-11-18 restricted NightRealm save-code probe

Built a minimal standalone Unity player using NightRealm's byte-identical generic SaveLoadHandler, a copy of FileNameData patched to use a disposable root, synthetic data classes and stubs for unused wrapped-object dependencies. The source handler SHA-256 is c0ddcd6ed7d6a3b72fb71ec2f5559894f4b2e0d5ea9d9127b4468fd157c5be30. An unrestricted control and no-capability AppContainer run each exited 0; in each the supervisor inspected two synthetic input files and two handler-written output files and verified matching parsed contents. The restricted run had an AppContainer token, no outside canary, zero active job processes and successful profile deletion; the control wrote the outside canary. The restricted outside write raised DirectoryNotFoundException, which does not establish broad isolation. This is not a game scene, real gameplay restore, wrapped inventory, historical save or production integration, and the worker can forge its own output. The full NightRealm Editor remains unable to start its Package Manager IPC under the attempted profile. See `results/GDM-001/real-game-integration-study-2026-11-18.md`. Next: integrate actual game components and a verified disposable complete save root in an appropriately contained build, then compare native and prototype workflows independently.


### 2026-11-18 original NightRealm level component probe

Built a minimal Windows Unity player containing byte-identical NightRealm `PlayerLevelSystem.cs` (SHA-256 `f3e6ac54b91f44e5485487dec04f104a57718e40a7aeb44474c577d397a43569`) and its generic save handler, with a redirected disposable save root and substitutes for the component's stats, audio, pooling and events. A no-capability AppContainer run restored level 2 / XP 7 from a synthetic PlayerLevel file, exiting 0. In a separate restricted run the original component saved and reloaded that state; XP became 2, reported `player.currentXp`, and exited 1. An unrestricted control reproduced the same behavior. The supervisor independently inspected before/after save bytes, verified expected values, confirmed restricted tokens and absent outside canaries, observed no active job processes, and deleted both restricted profiles. This reproduces the source-level XP issue in an isolated component harness, not in the full game scene or an historical save. No upstream changes or reports were made. See `results/GDM-001/real-game-integration-study-2026-11-18.md`. Next: actual scene and inventory restoration under a verified boundary; independent developer still unavailable.

## Execution persistence for this project

When the owner asks you to work on this project, continue autonomously through all remaining authorized tasks possible with available access and resources. Do not stop merely because a few minutes passed, after one task, a plan, or a progress update. Continue implementation, appropriate verification, evidence recording, and the next actionable task until the requested work is finished or no further authorized work can be performed. Give progress updates without ending longer work. If authorization, access, payment, another person, or external state blocks an action, complete independent authorized work first, then checkpoint and report the precise blocker and next action. Preserve completed progress, financial evidence, and uncertain external effects; respect existing scope, budget, permissions, and safety controls. Never claim unverified completion.

# Advanced Capacity-Aware NPC Transport System — Complete Business and Implementation Plan

## 1. Executive decision and current status

**Decision: retain as a differentiated but niche, unvalidated gameplay-system candidate.** Build an engine-integrated passenger *journey coordinator*, not another general pathfinder or elevator motion asset. It handles scheduled finite-capacity vehicles, stations, queue discipline, seat allocation, transfers, missed departures, disruptions and reliable save/load with multiple NPCs.

- **Exact buyer:** small Godot simulation, colony, factory, hospital, transport, school or city-builder studios that already have NPC movement and need multiple agents to share transport resources.
- **Buying trigger:** a game design requires NPCs to queue for elevators/ferries/buses and recover from changes; wiring navigation, reservations and persistence together is costly.
- **First technical edition:** **Godot 4 3D** with an original, readable GDScript state-machine core. This selection is for the *shortest credible initial local proof*; the first paid channel must be checked independently. Do not automatically promise 2D or Unity.
- **First paid route candidate:** itch.io or existing Payhip direct checkout; the official Godot Asset Store currently accepts free listings only. Revenue must not be assumed from a free asset listing.
- **Commercial state:** no observed sales, licensed demo, tested game adapter or benchmark. The scope below is a **proposed** integration product, not a completed plugin.
- **Deciding experiment:** compare native Godot navigation links and FlowAI against a local twenty-agent/two-vehicle transport schedule. If our component saves no meaningful implementation/QA effort, reject or narrow the family.

## 2. Repository baseline, duplicate analysis and reuse

`Hi62384/Proj`, `main`, commit `6f2a420e9a1d7d5b44ec1759918e737059a6772e` inspected 2026-11-15. The existing canonical project is `business_portfolio/niches/digital-products/game-development-marketplaces/projects/gdm-002-capacity-aware-npc-transport/project.md`, project ID `GDM-002`, niche `N-gdm-20261115`. Preserve active projects `GDM-001` and `GDM-003`; their actual jobs differ. Archive/research locations: `business_portfolio/archive/2026-11-15-legacy`, `archive/2026-11-15-taxonomy-view-v1` and `opportunity_library`. Do not create a new ID, new niche, duplicate project, or touch another chat's owned files.

The repo contains no **verified implemented GDM-002 package** in the inspected public business record. Codex must search the current *local* repo for existing game AI/transport code before making a new module; the user has unrelated Godot game work outside this business portfolio, which cannot be assumed to be licensed for commercial reuse. Reuse only code/assets with proven rights and isolation. Shared test-vector descriptions and the project's prior state-machine research are legitimate planning assets.

## 3. Reassessment of nearby products and why this one survives conditionally

The previous 33-direction game-marketplace research narrowed to three active projects; this is a revision of GDM-002 rather than a new opportunity contest. The differentiation is **complete passenger lifecycle + recovery + integration into an existing controller**. It is not "more realistic graphics" or "50,000 agents".

| Alternative | Observed capabilities (source) | Why we might still be distinct | Kill signal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Native Godot NavigationLink / signals | Navigation can connect areas; movement/behavior still belongs to game logic. [Godot NavigationLink docs](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/navigation/navigation_using_navigationlinks.html) | No ready-made passenger reservations, guaranteed capacity, transfers or in-transit persistence assumed. | Buyer can add it with a trivial script. |
| Free FlowAI for Godot 4 | Moving graph areas can follow ships/elevators. [FlowAI](https://github.com/a6xdev/FlowAI) | We coordinate schedule/capacity/state on top of existing navigation. | FlowAI already has a direct equivalent passenger workflow in the required version. |
| Unity Marchline (future edition competitor) | Deterministic crowds, door capacity, queues, multi-storey, save/load. [Unity listing](https://assetstore.unity.com/packages/tools/behavior-ai/marchline-rts-pathfinding-crowd-navigation-400596) | NOT a claim of low Unity competition. A port would need unique vehicle/passenger itinerary functions. | Its use in the buyer's game is already sufficient. |
| Generic elevator/moving-platform scripts | Move between floors and synchronize doors. | Do not generally model shared queues, transfers and recovery. | A moving platform actually meets this buyer's full use case. |
| Large all-in-one city simulation toolkit | May already provide vehicles/riders. | Our system integrates with *existing* NPC AI rather than replacing it. | Adapter cost exceeds DIY or toolkit adoption. |

**Market evidence limit:** a developer forum describes elevator wait/board/exit needs; this is an engineering problem signal, not a measured paid market. Unity Marchline proves *competition*, not our demand. No credible number of Godot buyers, conversion rate, or unit sales is known. Godot-first is a **technical experiment**, subject to paid-route/customer reachability.

## 4. Buyer/job-to-be-done and reasons not to purchase

Buyer A is developing a hospital/office building with multiple floors and NPCs sharing lifts. Buyer B has a colony simulation with ferries/buses on timed routes. They need reliable agent progression: request route → wait for transport → reserve capacity → board exactly once → ride → transfer/exit → arrive or recover with an understandable reason. The system should not demand replacement of their existing movement or quest AI.

Nonbuyers: games with one player-triggered lift, games without persistent NPC populations, teams already running a purpose-built passenger coordinator, developers who need road vehicle physics/networked traffic from day one, customers unable to provide stable agent and stop identifiers.

**Why buy versus AI?** A quick AI-generated queue can work in one demonstration, but event ordering, last-seat races, cancellations, save/restore at every transition and interoperable diagnostics require many tests and maintenance. The product only deserves a price if its tested implementation and integration API measurably reduce engineering and debugging effort.

## 5. First useful commercial edition — no overbuilding

### Must ship

1. One complete Godot 4 3D addon with a transport graph (`Stop`, `Service`, `Vehicle`), deterministic scheduler, seat ledger, station queues and agent journey state machine.
2. A simple integration API: register stops/vehicles, request/cancel journeys, notify a boarding/movement callback, receive transport events and serialize/restore state.
3. Configurable small multi-stop elevator/ferry/bus *behavior presets* using the same capacity engine—not simulated traffic physics or a full vehicle model. At least one reliable moving 3D platform demo.
4. End-to-end journey from external NPC navigation through wait/board/ride/transfer/arrival, with clearly defined delays, failures and rerouting.
5. Reproducible save/load snapshots including mid-queue and mid-boarding state, deterministic event IDs and a debugger that explains every agent's waiting reason.
6. Bounded performance fixture: initially **20 agents, two capacity-limited vehicles and one transfer**, then measure on a pinned PC and Godot version. Do not advertise capacity larger than actually tested.
7. Source, demo project, API reference, integration recipes for two movement-controller patterns, troubleshooting guide, supported versions, licensing and QA report.

### Excluded from first sale

Unrestricted multiplayer replication, Roblox server economies, dynamic rail/road construction, physics/traffic simulation, all movement controllers, unrestricted train timetables, 10,000 agents, procedural map generation, visual editors for every topology, universal engine compatibility and fully autonomous crowds. These are separate products/features requiring proven demand. Animations and 3D meshes are replaceable demonstration assets; do not promise high-end artwork.

| Engine | Candidate edition / market feasibility | Proposed next action |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot 4 3D** | **Chosen for local proof**, direct paid sales; official Godot store free-only at this review. | Demonstrate actual capacity/transfer/recovery and verify paid-channel discovery. |
| Godot 2D | Different movement signals and navigation integration. | Port only after demonstrated 3D traction or stronger independent buyer evidence. |
| Unity 3D/2D | Marchline and many crowd/lift products; competition substantial. | Evaluate specific *vehicle itinerary* gap, not a broad navigation rewrite. |
| Unreal Engine | Blueprint/C++ plugin and Smart Objects/lift products. | Re-assess against Fab's current paid systems before any port. |
| Roblox | Server-authoritative reservations, replication, disconnections and abuse cases. | Independent edition; not a trivial module conversion. |
| GameMaker | 2D room/path/instance model, save compatibility to test. | Needs viable SDK and marketplace pathway. |
| Construct / GDevelop | Event/extension architectures and distribution rules differ. | Feasibility/reachability only; reject when integration is costly. |

A shared **behavior contract and test fixtures** can be reused; cross-engine source may need complete reimplementation. Do not count port listings as sales or separate businesses.

## 6. Competition and evidence ledger

| Source | Verified information / limitation | Review |
|---|---|---|
| [Godot forum elevator pathfinding question](https://forum.godotengine.org/t/pathfinding-with-elevator-platform/45444) | Documents a concrete wait/board/ride/exit problem, **not** willingness to pay. | 2026-11-15 research review |
| [FlowAI repository](https://github.com/a6xdev/FlowAI) | Moving pathnode graph/area can follow lifts or ships; no claim that its listed capabilities are incomplete without testing. | 2026-11-15 |
| [Godot NavigationLink](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/navigation/navigation_using_navigationlinks.html) | Native navigation links are baseline primitives. | 2026-11-15 |
| [Unity Marchline listing](https://assetstore.unity.com/packages/tools/behavior-ai/marchline-rts-pathfinding-crowd-navigation-400596) | Advertises capacity-limited passages, queues, cross-floor routing and saved queue state; high overlap for a Unity edition. | 2026-11-15 |
| [Godot official store FAQ](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/community/asset_store/faq.html) | Paid assets not available on official store currently; future plans are not current revenue. | 2026-11-15 |
| [Payhip pricing](https://payhip.com/pricing) | Free seller plan lists 5% platform fee *plus separate card/PayPal processor fees*. | 2026-11-15 |

These sources do not establish how many people would purchase *this* system. Search current Godot/itch.io competitors again immediately before a paid listing. If a complete existing passenger transport addon already satisfies this specification for less, stop rather than copy it.

## 7. Competitive baseline and bounded proof without interviews

**Owner revision, 2026-11-18:** The comparative test is informative, not a stop condition for local development or testing. Preserve and report the observed DIY overlap and do not claim an advantage without evidence. All release-quality checks and separate owner approval for publication remain required.

Construct **two** demos in the same original Godot project. A baseline uses NavigationAgent/NavigationLink plus a minimal custom queue script; the proposed addon uses the transport core and two different movement-controller adapters. Record how many edge cases fail in baseline, implementation time, code modification burden and repeatable restart behavior. The original proposed differentiation criterion was more reliable scheduled reservation and mid-ride save/recovery with less integration effort; this remains an evidence standard for any such claim, not a blocker to local development. No survey or team evaluation is required.

**Original risk signals (no longer a mandatory stop for local development under the owner revision):** if adding a FIFO array to a moving platform solves all target uses at lower complexity; if save/restore is inconsistent; if controllers need invasive rewrites; if paid checkout/discovery cannot be established affordably; or if support effort is disproportionate. Production polish alone does not rescue a missing market.

## 8. Business model and first CAD150/month economics

**Proposed direct digital download:** CAD79 initial price experiment, one-time engine-edition license with versioned updates under a stated support policy; license and actual checkout price require owner approval. Prefer use of the repo's existing store infrastructure only if license/redistribution and merchant-of-record terms work. No subscription, paid backend or per-seat billing infrastructure in v1.

**Illustrative unit math:** Payhip free seller fee is currently 5% (source above). *Assume*, do not claim as sourced, payment processing 3% + CAD0.35 per completed order, refund allowance 5% of gross, CAD0 hosting/ads/new tooling. Per completed CAD79 order, provisional contribution before owner labor = `79 × (1 - 0.05 - 0.03 - 0.05) - 0.35 = CAD68.38`. Actual payment provider fees, FX/tax and refund rules must be checked.

| Monthly scenario | Hypothetical paid orders | Gross CAD | Fee/reserve total CAD | Contribution CAD | CAD150 portfolio target share |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Stress | 0 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0% |
| Base hypothesis | 2 | 158.00 | 21.24 | 136.76 | 91.2% |
| Upside hypothesis | 5 | 395.00 | 53.10 | 341.90 | 227.9% |

**Three orders** in a month would yield approximately CAD205.14 under these unverified assumptions; one successful month is not automatically recurring. With CAD0 upfront, the first positive order is nominal cash break-even before owner labor. If a planned CAD60 cost were separately approved, break-even would require one paid order at the assumed unit contribution. If refund/processing/marketplace total variable deductions rise to 25% plus CAD0.35, each CAD79 sale yields CAD58.90 and three orders are still needed for CAD150. A one-order month yields CAD68.38, so the product can contribute partially toward the **portfolio-wide** goal.

**Effort hypothesis:** 35–75 focused AI-assisted engineering and QA hours; 2–6 hours of owner review/approval; after release ~1–3 hours/month maintenance plus incident support (not observed). Worst-case revenue is CAD0 while engineering and maintenance consume time. If support averages 2 hours *per* CAD79 sale, it may be economically unattractive even with positive cash contribution. Do not hide owner labor in a positive margin number.

## 9. Distribution, listing drafts and organic launch

**Primary paid route:** itch.io/direct download or existing Payhip checkout after owner-approved account/licensing setup. **Do not** place the full paid source in the official free Godot store. A genuinely free, separable tutorial/demo is an optional discovery channel *only if its license and the official store rules are compatible*; don't give away paid functionality unintentionally. Fab/Unity Asset Store are relevant only once genuine engine editions exist and qualify under those stores.

**Qualified search terms to test (not measured search volume):** `Godot NPC elevator queue`, `Godot ferry NPC boarding`, `Godot passenger transport simulation`, `Godot AI transport network`, `Godot save queue lift addon`.

**Draft title:** *Passenger Transit Coordinator for Godot — Queues, Capacity, Transfers and Save/Load*.

**Draft teaser:** *Let NPCs take scheduled lifts and transport without overbooking, duplicate boarding, or losing their place after a save/load. Integrate with your movement controller; visualize the journey and recover from delays.*

**Main demo storyboard:** 20 differently colored NPC markers compete for two transport vehicles; an NPC misses a transfer; a vehicle goes out of service; midway through boarding, save and reload; HUD shows occupancy, queue length and journey state; replay final outcome and show no duplicate seat. Capture real software footage only after QA. Provide an original sample Godot project, integration gif/video, explanatory diagrams and an API checklist. Licensing must not overpromise multiplayer or all NPC controller types.

**Launch sequence:** build scenario replay → capture authentic demonstration → make paid sample and setup docs → prepare product cover/thumbs → compare direct checkout usability and store discoverability → owner-approve any account/publication actions → publish → record genuine page visits and sales → adjust pricing or demo based on observed bottleneck. Ads remain CAD0 absent later authorization and conversion evidence.

## 10. Architecture: pure transport rules plus engine adapters

**First edition design:** GDScript for Godot 4 with a deterministic simulation tick and minimal Node-facing adapter. Navigation and rendered movement remain owned by the customer. The core must not depend on scene hierarchy, 3D animations or external networking; use explicit callback events from the controller.

```text
Proposed source tree (not yet built):
products/game-tools/capacity-aware-npc-transport/
  addons/transit_coordinator/plugin.cfg
  addons/transit_coordinator/core/{transit_graph,route_planner,schedule_clock}.gd
  addons/transit_coordinator/core/{seat_ledger,queue_policy,journey_machine,event_journal}.gd
  addons/transit_coordinator/contracts/{transport_config,journey_result,snapshot_schema}.gd
  addons/transit_coordinator/adapters/{movement_adapter_3d,navigation_link_adapter}.gd
  addons/transit_coordinator/editor/{transit_inspector,network_gizmo,config_validator}.gd
  demo/{project.godot,worlds,scenes,scripts,assets}
  tests/unit/{ledger_test,queue_test,planner_test,snapshot_test}.gd
  tests/integration/{lift_transfer_test,disruption_test,controller_adapter_test}.gd
  tests/fixtures/{two_vehicle_trace,restoration_trace,disabled_service_trace}.json
  docs/{quickstart,api,controller_adapters,save_restore,version_support,limitations}.md
  tools/{run_fixture.py,package.py,verify_release.py}
  LICENSE, CHANGELOG.md, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md
```

**Ownership:** `transit_graph` is the source of stop/service edges and stable IDs. `route_planner` consumes graph + timetable and proposes legs but never allocates seats. `seat_ledger` is the **only seat allocator**, synchronized on one authoritative simulation tick. `journey_machine` orchestrates agent state; `event_journal` deduplicates each transition; `snapshot_schema` persists exact state; adapters issue/acknowledge movement but cannot change core occupancy. View/UI are read-only projections and never own reservations.

**Configuration requirements:** stable `stop_id`, `service_id`, `vehicle_id`, `agent_id` strings; versioned service schedule, stop order, capacity >=1, dwell/departure times, queue discipline, deadlines and required agent movement callbacks. Validate missing endpoints, duplicate identifiers, nonpositive capacity, cyclic zero-time schedules, unreachable legs and timezone/unit mismatch. Simulation time is integer ticks, not wall-clock milliseconds.

## 11. State machine, schemas, algorithms and invariants

**Journey states:** `requested → routing → walking_to_stop → queued → reserved → boarding → onboard → alighting → transfer_waiting → completed`; side transitions to `rerouting`, `cancelled`, `failed`. Event IDs are stable `run_id:tick:vehicle_id:sequence` or another collision-safe deterministic scheme. Saved state includes current leg index, queue ticket, seat claim, boarded vehicle, last processed event and schedule tick.

**Immutable invariants:** for every vehicle, `0 <= occupied_seats <= capacity`; no agent in two vehicle seats; no agent simultaneously marked queued and onboard; a seat claim is owned by exactly one agent; reprocessing the same event ID changes nothing; cancellation cannot create a later boarding; snapshot load reconstructs identical eventual state under identical inputs.

**Public proposed API:**

```gdscript
var journey = transit.request_journey(agent_id, destination_stop_id, options)
transit.cancel_journey(journey.id)
transit.register_vehicle(vehicle_id, route_id, capacity)
transit.notify_arrived_at_stop(agent_id, stop_id)
transit.acknowledge_boarded(agent_id, vehicle_id, event_id)
transit.acknowledge_disembarked(agent_id, vehicle_id, event_id)
var state = transit.serialize_snapshot() # versioned data, NOT scene nodes
transit.restore_snapshot(state)
# Signals: journey_changed, boarding_requested, vehicle_departed, service_disrupted
```

All APIs above are **proposals**, not confirmed GDScript implementations; specify true Godot types once engine version is pinned.

**Route planning (bounded deterministic Dijkstra/time-dependent graph):** a node is `(stop_id, arrival_tick)`; edges include walk or service departure with wait and ride time; compute earliest feasible itinerary given current schedule; tie-break by stable service/stop ID. Before boarding, journey state machine asks ledger for seat claim. If no capacity, queue by `(priority_class, request_tick, agent_id)` to avoid nondeterministic race. A missed departure invalidates only that leg and triggers replanning; do not strand other agents. For large recurrent schedules, cache schedule indexes only after correctness passes.

```text
on_tick(T):
    collect input events; stable_sort by (tick, priority, vehicle_id, agent_id, event_id)
    ignore event_id if processed; emit typed 'duplicate_event_ignored'
    advance departures/arrivals and close boarding windows
    for vehicle: allocate free seats FIFO to eligible waiting agents
    for boarding ACK: verify active reserved seat+same vehicle, then commit occupancy once
    for cancellation or disruption: release claims, journal cause, reroute affected agents
    publish immutable state view and diagnostic reason codes
```

**Atomicity rule:** one authoritative event loop owns ledger writes; no thread can directly mutate seats. A boarding reservation is a *claim*, not occupancy; occupancy commits on acknowledgment. If a callback never arrives by timeout, release claim safely. If boarding animation finishes after cancellation, reject stale ACK and request adapter recovery. A save taken between reservation and animation persists a clearly identified `reserved` or `boarding` state and restores it once. Restore validates graph revisions and runs a migration function only for explicitly supported snapshot versions; unsupported versions return an error, not a quietly reset world.

**Proposed snapshot excerpt:**

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1, "tick": 240, "graph_version": "demo-v1",
  "vehicles": [{"id":"lift-a", "capacity":2, "occupied":["npc-02"], "claimed":["npc-03"]}],
  "journeys": [{"agent":"npc-03", "state":"boarding", "vehicle":"lift-a",
                "current_leg":1, "queue_ticket":"ticket-37", "last_event":"demo:240:lift-a:4"}],
  "processed_event_ids": ["demo:239:lift-a:3"]
}
```

The example is a schema sketch; snapshots must never trust the `occupied` list without enforcing capacity, uniqueness and version validation. Use compact event retention with a proven safe replay window; do not store unbounded event IDs forever in a production game.

**Performance target:** first demonstration 20 NPCs/two vehicles with deterministic replay. Record elapsed simulation time per tick, queue length, outstanding reservations and allocation operations on a specified Windows PC and pinned Godot build. No 1,000-agent performance claim until a real measured fixture establishes it.

## 13. Test fixtures and release-blocking QA

| Fixture / situation | Expected result |
|---|---|
| Two agents request the final seat during one tick | Exactly one successful claim; second remains queued with reason `capacity_full`. |
| One agent cancels while reserved | Claim released once; late boarding callback rejected; next in queue eligible. |
| Boarding ACK duplicated after restore | Only one occupancy transition, one ticket used, one journal event committed. |
| Vehicle departs before another agent arrives | Missed-trip condition; new feasible route or explicit failed/unreachable status. |
| Vehicle breaks down mid-ride | Rider transitions to defined waiting/rerouting/failed, never silently vanishes. |
| Stop becomes inaccessible during transfer | Replan or terminate with reason, preserve other trips. |
| Agent changes destination twice | Older request canceled; no leaked queue ticket or seat. |
| Save in `boarding` and reload | Identical seat/queue ownership, eventually same state under same replay. |
| Restore snapshot with `occupied > capacity` | Reject invalid snapshot; do not spawn overlapping passenger state. |
| Two controllers move at different speeds | Core remains correct; adapters correctly signal stop arrival/board/exit. |
| Cyclic route with no service | Planner terminates bounded; returns explicit no-route, no infinite loop. |
| Scene closed while NPC awaiting | Cleanup releases reservations and emits diagnostics. |

**Run guidance (after implementation):** `godot --headless --path <DEMO_PROJECT> --script <TEST_RUNNER_SCRIPT>` and `godot --headless --path <DEMO_PROJECT> --quit-after <TICKS>` are **proposed** examples; Codex must verify the installed Godot command-line flags and actual script paths. ## 16. Post-release operations and customer support

- Publish a clear supported version matrix; request *reproducible, redacted* bug reports rather than sensitive project archives. Disclose current limitations; do not promise unlimited bespoke integrations at the base price.
- Triage: verify report/version → reproduce on minimal fixture → classify `supported bug`, `integration`, `unsupported use`, or `feature request` → provide workaround/patch → regression-test all prior fixtures → version release. Preserve previous packages for rollback.
- Maintenance cost is uncertain. Reserve an illustrative 0.5–2 hours/month per product plus 0.25–1 hour per meaningful support incident, **not** a measured commitment. If the real load materially exceeds this, revise economics, reduce supported configurations or pause expansion.
- Collect no product telemetry by default. Use actual accessible marketplace analytics and private support records without placing personal customer data in this public project record.

## 17. Performance measurement, portfolio decisions, and future products

Measure after actual publication: direct store product views where available, download and demo completion counts when legitimate, orders, price/discount applied, real payment fees, refunds, bug categories, supported Godot versions, time spent helping users. Record the date, currency, fee deductions, refunded transactions, hours of support and net contribution in the appropriate authorized private financial systems; report only non-sensitive aggregates publicly. A pageview is not a sale and a listing favorite is not a verified purchase.

Decision heuristics (not statistical proof): **continue** if actual positive net contribution and low support persist; **improve** when a specific demo, pricing, installation or discovery weakness can be addressed in a bounded update; **expand** only if there is proven traction plus a justified additional engine/channel; **pause** if exposure is tiny and costs are near-zero; **discontinue** if a free/native passenger queue example is sufficient for the identified buyer, an already available paid addon provides the same end-to-end function, or integration into ordinary NPC controllers costs more than DIY. Do not infer a bad idea solely from zero sales without evidence that qualified customers saw it.

## 18. Adversarial review and kill conditions

The strongest reasons the business could fail are: the target market for intricate passenger AI may be small; the first paid channel may be discoverability-poor; free FlowAI/navigation tools and paid Unity crowd systems already overlap; open-ended support requests could consume the revenue. Before implementation, run a *free/AI DIY challenge*: reproduce the promised result using native engine tools, a public alternative and a short AI-assisted script. Record setup time, bug count and diagnostic quality for the same fixtures. If the new tool has no real advantage, cut the scope or stop—no rebranding a duplicate as a new project.

Other fail conditions: insufficient legally permitted distribution, accuracy/privacy defects, platform/SDK changes exceeding support economics, or the release depending on paid/forbidden services outside the authorized budget. No human interviews or paid pilots are mandatory. Technical QA and official permission gates remain mandatory.
