# AWA-079 — Jobsite photo to caption draft

## Decision and evidence
**Classification:** standalone_service. **Priority:** P3. **Commercial state:** unvalidated. A separately commissioned deliverable is plausible, but it is one offer within a service business, not proof of an independent market.

At least one comparable buyer request was found. That request is not an agreement with this user and may involve a different scope, budget or level of experience. Priority is editorial sequencing for fast, low-upfront-cost experimentation, not probability of success. No workflow implementation, client interview, proposal, contract, paid order or production test was performed for this candidate in this package.

## Buyer, trigger and reason to pay
**Buyer:** HVAC or trades marketing agency with approved jobsite images.

**Problem/outcome:** A draft social caption and evidence link ready for editorial approval.

**Buying trigger:** A real team loses track of approved assets, versions and feedback between its existing storage and review systems.

A defensible fee is for resolving the buyer’s specific mapping/operating problem, measured acceptance, failure handling and usable handover—not for owning a template or merely using AI. Ask for one real failure example and the operational consequence. If native configuration or vendor support solves it adequately, use that cheaper route or decline the custom build.

**Native/free/AI alternatives:** Native content queues, DAM/PM approval tools and existing AI drafting tools handle much of the basic work.

## Bounded deliverable
Watch authorized Drive review folder; select approved images; generate caption candidates; assign editor.

**Pilot cap:** One approved Drive folder, one caption format and one review queue.

Include a versioned field/rule map, sanitized export where permitted, test results, known limitations, rollback/recovery instructions and customer-owned handover. Changes outside the cap need a new estimate. No external publication, unsolicited messaging, payments/refunds, destructive data changes or account-wide permissions are implied.

## Acceptance and implementation sequence
1. Confirm the current behavior, ownership, destination semantics and one named acceptance decision-maker. Use synthetic/redacted fixtures before requesting production access.
2. Specify the smallest deterministic implementation. Introduce AI only when text variability justifies it; keep a review/abstention path and budget approval.
3. Draft never invents results or personal details; nothing publishes without approval.
4. **Distinct failure test:** A photo cannot authorize disclosure of a house number, face, private site or unverified work claim; publication stays manual.
5. Verify outputs independently of a tool’s “success” response. Test permission loss, retries and partial failures relevant to this scope. Record observed results, residual limitations and restore instructions.
6. Obtain customer acceptance and hand over/revoke temporary access. Do not mark a mock test as a production pass.

**Required access/environment:** One permissioned asset folder, explicit asset rights and a human reviewer; AI credits only if separately authorized. Production belongs in an appropriately authorized customer-owned account and reliable hosting, not a dependency on the owner’s laptop staying awake. For n8n use cases, check P02 before offering hosted/external configuration access.

## Economics and remaining human work
**New customer-price hypothesis:** CAD250–450 for the stated cap; this is not the owner's startup cost, an observed sale or a conversion of earlier USD ideas. The `historical_price_usd_hypothesis` field, where present, preserves the prior unvalidated USD idea; it is not the current quote. Customer willingness to pay this CAD quote is unverified.

**Efficiency change:** Use existing tools and a fixed style brief; no posting automation or new AI subscription by default.

**Time boundaries:** stop unpaid preparation/qualification for this experiment at four owner-hours total, including the proof; do not build eight custom demos for eight requests. Aim for at most a 60–90 minute reusable fictional proof. The proposed paid delivery allowance is at most 5 hours, including testing and handover, followed by 30–60 minutes of defined defect triage. These are workload limits to validate, not promises that unfamiliar integration work fits them. Quote separately or decline before accepting work that does not fit. Do not omit necessary testing to stay inside the cap.

| Scenario, not forecast | Receipt | Fees / refund reserve assumptions | Allocated cash | All owner hours | Contribution before owner labor/tax | Effective hourly contribution |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Favorable direct at lower quote | CAD250 | 5% combined processing, 0% refund reserve | CAD0 | 7.5 | CAD237.50 | CAD31.67 |
| Marketplace stress at lower quote | CAD250 | 20% fee, 5% refund reserve | CAD25 | 10.5 | CAD162.50 | CAD15.48 |

The favorable scenario allocates one proof hour, one acquisition hour and half an hour of support on top of the delivery cap. The stress case allocates 1.5 proof hours, three acquisition hours and one support hour. Include previous failed pitches and shared business-development time in actual results; they can exceed both examples. The fee percentages are sensitivity assumptions, not assertions of any provider's exact rate. A 20% marketplace case is deliberately conservative; verify the actual provider and contract.

At an illustrative CAD30/hour owner-time target, the stress scenario needs about **CAD453.33** in customer price to break even economically. This is a rejection test, not permission to claim a buyer will pay that price. If that floor exceeds the credible quote, narrow the deliverable without weakening acceptance, use a less costly acquisition channel, or decline. Zero customers produces zero receipts and loses the time/cash spent.

**Unavoidable human work:** qualification, proof of skill, access decisions, scope agreement, ambiguous exceptions, independent acceptance, handover, support and payment reconciliation. Do not call the offer passive. Full methodology: [economics](../../../../../../research/ECONOMICS_V2.md).

## Customer acquisition and validation gate
### Buyer and buying trigger
A marketing operator with existing tools and approved content who needs technical reliability, not guaranteed conversions. A request must actually match **turn permitted jobsite photos into drafts that a person can check**; broad interest in AI is not enough.

### Positioning and proof
**Landing/profile headline draft:** Turn permitted jobsite photos into drafts that a person can check.

**Show, rather than claim:** A small permitted photo set produces labeled drafts with unverifiable details omitted. Label all examples fictional. Show actual observed test results only after running them. Keep one relevant annotated screenshot or a 45–90 second demo and a one-page scope; no new website, logo, CRM or subscription is required.

**One-call-to-action draft:** “Send a redacted example of the current problem and the result you need. I will confirm whether it fits this fixed scope before proposing paid work.” This is draft copy, not a message sent.

**Response draft for an invited, eligible buyer request:** “Your request mentions [their exact failure]. My proposed deliverable is: turn permitted jobsite photos into drafts that a person can check. The check I would use is: a small permitted photo set produces labeled drafts with unverifiable details omitted. I would first verify whether your existing tools can do this natively. The bounded scope excludes [the project exclusions below]. Are you able to share a redacted example and name the person who will accept the result? I would confirm scope, access and a fixed quote before starting.” Remove any implication of prior client results; do not claim unearned certification.

### $0-first acquisition experiment
Respond only to relevant, current invited implementation requests or a genuine opt-in referral; use one approved professional profile post as secondary discovery.

**Specific discovery phrase:** `jobsite photos caption drafting approval workflow`. Check current date, location restrictions, budget, exact deliverable, reputation/credential requirements and whether hiring is still open. Search results and community categories are lead-discovery starting points, not a vetted live prospect list.

Prepare at most eight high-fit request records in two batches of four. Obtain owner approval before responses or public posts. Use one reusable proof and personalize the problem, not a generic AI pitch. Stop at four unpaid owner-hours, eight eligible attempts or fourteen elapsed calendar days—whichever comes first—and review what happened. A time-box is not a promised time to first revenue. Pause earlier when no eligible request exists; do not purchase exposure merely to fill a quota.

**Secondary channel:** one relevant, permitted public demonstration or a genuine opt-in referral. No unsolicited mass DMs, scraped email lists or automated applications. Upwork is optional only after eligibility and actual Connects costs are checked; its proposal expense is not assumed zero. Do not move marketplace-sourced pre-contract communication or payment off-platform contrary to its rules.

### Funnel, decision and sale
Record source, eligible request, authorized response, meaningful reply, scoped conversation, funded agreement, accepted delivery, collected receipt, refund and total owner time. Count unpaid likes, followers, waitlist entries and quotes separately from customers. With no meaningful replies after the first four qualified attempts, revise one of buyer/offer/proof before using the second batch; do not simply increase posting volume. With replies but no scoped agreement, record the objection. With no paid commitment at the cap, pause this offer instead of building more features. These are spending/workload gates, not statistical proof of market failure.

Do not begin client-specific production work until there is an agreed scope, lawful permissions, a funded milestone or approved payment arrangement and acceptance criteria. A small paid diagnosis can precede a repair; do not relabel free discovery as a paid deliverable. Ask for a case study or referral only after a real successful delivery and permission.

**Project-specific rejection:** No face identification, fabricated before/after results or unsupported safety claims.

### Advertising decision
**Current ad allocation: CAD0.** This narrow service needs proof and qualified conversations before broad paid traffic. Advertised job budgets do not establish conversion economics. Only reassess ads after actual profitable sales; any later test must have a measured conversion path, a conservative acquisition-cost ceiling and a separate approved total budget. No retargeting pixels, uploaded customer lists or campaign launch is authorized by this plan.

**Launch gate:** `buyer_test_only`. For skill-gated work, produce a convincing disposable-environment acceptance test before offering the service. For follow-ons, do not advertise before the earlier project actually has paying clients. # AWA-080 — Campaign asset approval queue

## Decision and evidence
**Classification:** standalone_service. **Priority:** P3. **Commercial state:** unvalidated. A separately commissioned deliverable is plausible, but it is one offer within a service business, not proof of an independent market.

The sources establish adjacent work or platform capabilities, not a verified exact-scope buyer for this entry. Validate the particular problem before offering or building it. Priority is editorial sequencing for fast, low-upfront-cost experimentation, not probability of success. No workflow implementation, client interview, proposal, contract, paid order or production test was performed for this candidate in this package.

## Buyer, trigger and reason to pay
**Buyer:** Small marketing firm sharing drafts across disjointed tools.

**Problem/outcome:** Reviewer gets a versioned list of assets awaiting decision.

**Buying trigger:** A real team loses track of approved assets, versions and feedback between its existing storage and review systems.

A defensible fee is for resolving the buyer’s specific mapping/operating problem, measured acceptance, failure handling and usable handover—not for owning a template or merely using AI. Ask for one real failure example and the operational consequence. If native configuration or vendor support solves it adequately, use that cheaper route or decline the custom build.

**Native/free/AI alternatives:** Native content queues, DAM/PM approval tools and existing AI drafting tools handle much of the basic work.

## Bounded deliverable
Read submitted link and creative metadata; create review ticket; record accept/revise.

**Pilot cap:** One creative submission form, one approver and one versioned decision.

Include a versioned field/rule map, sanitized export where permitted, test results, known limitations, rollback/recovery instructions and customer-owned handover. Changes outside the cap need a new estimate. No external publication, unsolicited messaging, payments/refunds, destructive data changes or account-wide permissions are implied.

## Acceptance and implementation sequence
1. Confirm the current behavior, ownership, destination semantics and one named acceptance decision-maker. Use synthetic/redacted fixtures before requesting production access.
2. Specify the smallest deterministic implementation. Introduce AI only when text variability justifies it; keep a review/abstention path and budget approval.
3. Stale asset version cannot silently replace approved version.
4. **Distinct failure test:** Approval is bound to the exact asset/version; a replaced file invalidates the earlier release approval.
5. Verify outputs independently of a tool’s “success” response. Test permission loss, retries and partial failures relevant to this scope. Record observed results, residual limitations and restore instructions.
6. Obtain customer acceptance and hand over/revoke temporary access. Do not mark a mock test as a production pass.

**Required access/environment:** One permissioned asset folder, explicit asset rights and a human reviewer; AI credits only if separately authorized. Production belongs in an appropriately authorized customer-owned account and reliable hosting, not a dependency on the owner’s laptop staying awake. For n8n use cases, check P02 before offering hosted/external configuration access.

## Economics and remaining human work
**New customer-price hypothesis:** CAD300–550 for the stated cap; this is not the owner's startup cost, an observed sale or a conversion of earlier USD ideas. The `historical_price_usd_hypothesis` field, where present, preserves the prior unvalidated USD idea; it is not the current quote. Customer willingness to pay this CAD quote is unverified.

**Efficiency change:** Use the existing PM/review tool and a simple version key.

**Time boundaries:** stop unpaid preparation/qualification for this experiment at four owner-hours total, including the proof; do not build eight custom demos for eight requests. Aim for at most a 60–90 minute reusable fictional proof. The proposed paid delivery allowance is at most 6 hours, including testing and handover, followed by 30–60 minutes of defined defect triage. These are workload limits to validate, not promises that unfamiliar integration work fits them. Quote separately or decline before accepting work that does not fit. Do not omit necessary testing to stay inside the cap.

| Scenario, not forecast | Receipt | Fees / refund reserve assumptions | Allocated cash | All owner hours | Contribution before owner labor/tax | Effective hourly contribution |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Favorable direct at lower quote | CAD300 | 5% combined processing, 0% refund reserve | CAD0 | 8.5 | CAD285.00 | CAD33.53 |
| Marketplace stress at lower quote | CAD300 | 20% fee, 5% refund reserve | CAD25 | 11.5 | CAD200.00 | CAD17.39 |

The favorable scenario allocates one proof hour, one acquisition hour and half an hour of support on top of the delivery cap. The stress case allocates 1.5 proof hours, three acquisition hours and one support hour. Include previous failed pitches and shared business-development time in actual results; they can exceed both examples. The fee percentages are sensitivity assumptions, not assertions of any provider's exact rate. A 20% marketplace case is deliberately conservative; verify the actual provider and contract.

At an illustrative CAD30/hour owner-time target, the stress scenario needs about **CAD493.33** in customer price to break even economically. This is a rejection test, not permission to claim a buyer will pay that price. If that floor exceeds the credible quote, narrow the deliverable without weakening acceptance, use a less costly acquisition channel, or decline. Zero customers produces zero receipts and loses the time/cash spent.

**Unavoidable human work:** qualification, proof of skill, access decisions, scope agreement, ambiguous exceptions, independent acceptance, handover, support and payment reconciliation. Do not call the offer passive. Full methodology: [economics](../../../../../../research/ECONOMICS_V2.md).

## Customer acquisition and validation gate
### Buyer and buying trigger
A marketing operator with existing tools and approved content who needs technical reliability, not guaranteed conversions. A request must actually match **route campaign assets to the right approver with version history**; broad interest in AI is not enough.

### Positioning and proof
**Landing/profile headline draft:** Route campaign assets to the right approver with version history.

**Show, rather than claim:** An edited approved asset becomes unapproved until the new version is reviewed. Label all examples fictional. Show actual observed test results only after running them. Keep one relevant annotated screenshot or a 45–90 second demo and a one-page scope; no new website, logo, CRM or subscription is required.

**One-call-to-action draft:** “Send a redacted example of the current problem and the result you need. I will confirm whether it fits this fixed scope before proposing paid work.” This is draft copy, not a message sent.

**Response draft for an invited, eligible buyer request:** “Your request mentions [their exact failure]. My proposed deliverable is: route campaign assets to the right approver with version history. The check I would use is: an edited approved asset becomes unapproved until the new version is reviewed. I would first verify whether your existing tools can do this natively. The bounded scope excludes [the project exclusions below]. Are you able to share a redacted example and name the person who will accept the result? I would confirm scope, access and a fixed quote before starting.” Remove any implication of prior client results; do not claim unearned certification.

### $0-first acquisition experiment
Respond only to relevant, current invited implementation requests or a genuine opt-in referral; use one approved professional profile post as secondary discovery.

**Specific discovery phrase:** `marketing asset approval workflow automation`. Check current date, location restrictions, budget, exact deliverable, reputation/credential requirements and whether hiring is still open. Search results and community categories are lead-discovery starting points, not a vetted live prospect list.

Prepare at most eight high-fit request records in two batches of four. Obtain owner approval before responses or public posts. Use one reusable proof and personalize the problem, not a generic AI pitch. Stop at four unpaid owner-hours, eight eligible attempts or fourteen elapsed calendar days—whichever comes first—and review what happened. A time-box is not a promised time to first revenue. Pause earlier when no eligible request exists; do not purchase exposure merely to fill a quota.

**Secondary channel:** one relevant, permitted public demonstration or a genuine opt-in referral. No unsolicited mass DMs, scraped email lists or automated applications. Upwork is optional only after eligibility and actual Connects costs are checked; its proposal expense is not assumed zero. Do not move marketplace-sourced pre-contract communication or payment off-platform contrary to its rules.

### Funnel, decision and sale
Record source, eligible request, authorized response, meaningful reply, scoped conversation, funded agreement, accepted delivery, collected receipt, refund and total owner time. Count unpaid likes, followers, waitlist entries and quotes separately from customers. With no meaningful replies after the first four qualified attempts, revise one of buyer/offer/proof before using the second batch; do not simply increase posting volume. With replies but no scoped agreement, record the objection. With no paid commitment at the cap, pause this offer instead of building more features. These are spending/workload gates, not statistical proof of market failure.

Do not begin client-specific production work until there is an agreed scope, lawful permissions, a funded milestone or approved payment arrangement and acceptance criteria. A small paid diagnosis can precede a repair; do not relabel free discovery as a paid deliverable. Ask for a case study or referral only after a real successful delivery and permission.

**Project-specific rejection:** No automatic publication, media buying or promise of ad performance.

### Advertising decision
**Current ad allocation: CAD0.** This narrow service needs proof and qualified conversations before broad paid traffic. Advertised job budgets do not establish conversion economics. Only reassess ads after actual profitable sales; any later test must have a measured conversion path, a conservative acquisition-cost ceiling and a separate approved total budget. No retargeting pixels, uploaded customer lists or campaign launch is authorized by this plan.

**Launch gate:** `buyer_test_only`. For skill-gated work, produce a convincing disposable-environment acceptance test before offering the service. For follow-ons, do not advertise before the earlier project actually has paying clients. 3. Conflicting instructions surfaced and duplicates folded without erasing provenance.
4. **Distinct failure test:** Contradictory feedback is preserved for a decision rather than silently merged into an impossible instruction.
5. Verify outputs independently of a tool’s “success” response. Test permission loss, retries and partial failures relevant to this scope. Record observed results, residual limitations and restore instructions.

**Required access/environment:** One permissioned asset folder, explicit asset rights and a human reviewer; AI credits only if separately authorized. Production belongs in an appropriately authorized customer-owned account and reliable hosting, not a dependency on the owner’s laptop staying awake. For n8n use cases, check P02 before offering hosted/external configuration access.

## Economics and remaining human work
**New customer-price hypothesis:** CAD250–450 for the stated cap; this is not the owner's startup cost, an observed sale or a conversion of earlier USD ideas. The `historical_price_usd_hypothesis` field, where present, preserves the prior unvalidated USD idea; it is not the current quote. Customer willingness to pay this CAD quote is unverified.

**Efficiency change:** Use native export plus deterministic grouping; AI summary optional and reviewed.

**Time boundaries:** stop unpaid preparation/qualification for this experiment at four owner-hours total, including the proof; do not build eight custom demos for eight requests. Aim for at most a 60–90 minute reusable fictional proof. The proposed paid delivery allowance is at most 5 hours, including testing and handover, followed by 30–60 minutes of defined defect triage. These are workload limits to validate, not promises that unfamiliar integration work fits them. Quote separately or decline before accepting work that does not fit. Do not omit necessary testing to stay inside the cap.

| Scenario, not forecast | Receipt | Fees / refund reserve assumptions | Allocated cash | All owner hours | Contribution before owner labor/tax | Effective hourly contribution |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Favorable direct at lower quote | CAD250 | 5% combined processing, 0% refund reserve | CAD0 | 7.5 | CAD237.50 | CAD31.67 |
| Marketplace stress at lower quote | CAD250 | 20% fee, 5% refund reserve | CAD25 | 10.5 | CAD162.50 | CAD15.48 |

The favorable scenario allocates one proof hour, one acquisition hour and half an hour of support on top of the delivery cap. The stress case allocates 1.5 proof hours, three acquisition hours and one support hour. Include previous failed pitches and shared business-development time in actual results; they can exceed both examples. The fee percentages are sensitivity assumptions, not assertions of any provider's exact rate. A 20% marketplace case is deliberately conservative; verify the actual provider and contract.

At an illustrative CAD30/hour owner-time target, the stress scenario needs about **CAD453.33** in customer price to break even economically. This is a rejection test, not permission to claim a buyer will pay that price. If that floor exceeds the credible quote, narrow the deliverable without weakening acceptance, use a less costly acquisition channel, or decline. Zero customers produces zero receipts and loses the time/cash spent.

**Unavoidable human work:** qualification, proof of skill, access decisions, scope agreement, ambiguous exceptions, independent acceptance, handover, support and payment reconciliation. Do not call the offer passive. Full methodology: [economics](../../../../../../research/ECONOMICS_V2.md).

## Customer acquisition and validation gate
### Buyer and buying trigger
A marketing operator with existing tools and approved content who needs technical reliability, not guaranteed conversions. A request must actually match **convert one feedback round into a checked revision list**; broad interest in AI is not enough.

### Positioning and proof
**Landing/profile headline draft:** Convert one feedback round into a checked revision list.

**Show, rather than claim:** Up to 20 comments retain asset/version links and conflicting feedback flags. Label all examples fictional. Show actual observed test results only after running them. Keep one relevant annotated screenshot or a 45–90 second demo and a one-page scope; no new website, logo, CRM or subscription is required.

**One-call-to-action draft:** “Send a redacted example of the current problem and the result you need. I will confirm whether it fits this fixed scope before proposing paid work.” This is draft copy, not a message sent.

**Response draft for an invited, eligible buyer request:** “Your request mentions [their exact failure]. My proposed deliverable is: convert one feedback round into a checked revision list. The check I would use is: up to 20 comments retain asset/version links and conflicting feedback flags. I would first verify whether your existing tools can do this natively. The bounded scope excludes [the project exclusions below]. Are you able to share a redacted example and name the person who will accept the result? I would confirm scope, access and a fixed quote before starting.” Remove any implication of prior client results; do not claim unearned certification.

### $0-first acquisition experiment
Respond only to relevant, current invited implementation requests or a genuine opt-in referral; use one approved professional profile post as secondary discovery.

**Specific discovery phrase:** `creative client feedback revision summary workflow`. Check current date, location restrictions, budget, exact deliverable, reputation/credential requirements and whether hiring is still open. Search results and community categories are lead-discovery starting points, not a vetted live prospect list.

Prepare at most eight high-fit request records in two batches of four. Obtain owner approval before responses or public posts. Use one reusable proof and personalize the problem, not a generic AI pitch. Stop at four unpaid owner-hours, eight eligible attempts or fourteen elapsed calendar days—whichever comes first—and review what happened. A time-box is not a promised time to first revenue. Pause earlier when no eligible request exists; do not purchase exposure merely to fill a quota.

**Secondary channel:** one relevant, permitted public demonstration or a genuine opt-in referral. No unsolicited mass DMs, scraped email lists or automated applications. Upwork is optional only after eligibility and actual Connects costs are checked; its proposal expense is not assumed zero. Do not move marketplace-sourced pre-contract communication or payment off-platform contrary to its rules.

### Funnel, decision and sale
Record source, eligible request, authorized response, meaningful reply, scoped conversation, funded agreement, accepted delivery, collected receipt, refund and total owner time. Count unpaid likes, followers, waitlist entries and quotes separately from customers. With no meaningful replies after the first four qualified attempts, revise one of buyer/offer/proof before using the second batch; do not simply increase posting volume. With replies but no scoped agreement, record the objection. With no paid commitment at the cap, pause this offer instead of building more features. These are spending/workload gates, not statistical proof of market failure.

Do not begin client-specific production work until there is an agreed scope, lawful permissions, a funded milestone or approved payment arrangement and acceptance criteria. A small paid diagnosis can precede a repair; do not relabel free discovery as a paid deliverable. Ask for a case study or referral only after a real successful delivery and permission.

**Project-specific rejection:** Do not resolve contradictory client instructions by guessing.

### Advertising decision
**Current ad allocation: CAD0.** This narrow service needs proof and qualified conversations before broad paid traffic. Advertised job budgets do not establish conversion economics. Only reassess ads after actual profitable sales; any later test must have a measured conversion path, a conservative acquisition-cost ceiling and a separate approved total budget. No retargeting pixels, uploaded customer lists or campaign launch is authorized by this plan.

**Launch gate:** `buyer_test_only`. For skill-gated work, produce a convincing disposable-environment acceptance test before offering the service. ## Economics and remaining human work
**New customer-price hypothesis:** CAD250–450 for the stated cap; this is not the owner's startup cost, an observed sale or a conversion of earlier USD ideas. The `historical_price_usd_hypothesis` field, where present, preserves the prior unvalidated USD idea; it is not the current quote. Customer willingness to pay this CAD quote is unverified.

**Efficiency change:** Inspect the form and native integration before adding a tracking platform.

**Time boundaries:** stop unpaid preparation/qualification for this experiment at four owner-hours total, including the proof; do not build eight custom demos for eight requests. Aim for at most a 60–90 minute reusable fictional proof. The proposed paid delivery allowance is at most 5 hours, including testing and handover, followed by 30–60 minutes of defined defect triage. These are workload limits to validate, not promises that unfamiliar integration work fits them. Quote separately or decline before accepting work that does not fit. Do not omit necessary testing to stay inside the cap.

| Scenario, not forecast | Receipt | Fees / refund reserve assumptions | Allocated cash | All owner hours | Contribution before owner labor/tax | Effective hourly contribution |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Favorable direct at lower quote | CAD250 | 5% combined processing, 0% refund reserve | CAD0 | 7.5 | CAD237.50 | CAD31.67 |
| Marketplace stress at lower quote | CAD250 | 20% fee, 5% refund reserve | CAD25 | 10.5 | CAD162.50 | CAD15.48 |

The favorable scenario allocates one proof hour, one acquisition hour and half an hour of support on top of the delivery cap. The stress case allocates 1.5 proof hours, three acquisition hours and one support hour. Include previous failed pitches and shared business-development time in actual results; they can exceed both examples. The fee percentages are sensitivity assumptions, not assertions of any provider's exact rate. A 20% marketplace case is deliberately conservative; verify the actual provider and contract.

At an illustrative CAD30/hour owner-time target, the stress scenario needs about **CAD453.33** in customer price to break even economically. This is a rejection test, not permission to claim a buyer will pay that price. If that floor exceeds the credible quote, narrow the deliverable without weakening acceptance, use a less costly acquisition channel, or decline. Zero customers produces zero receipts and loses the time/cash spent.

**Unavoidable human work:** qualification, proof of skill, access decisions, scope agreement, ambiguous exceptions, independent acceptance, handover, support and payment reconciliation. Do not call the offer passive. Full methodology: [economics](../../../../../../research/ECONOMICS_V2.md).

## Customer acquisition and validation gate
### Buyer and buying trigger
A marketing operator with existing tools and approved content who needs technical reliability, not guaranteed conversions. A request must actually match **find lead-source labels that disappear before reaching the crm**; broad interest in AI is not enough.

### Positioning and proof
**Landing/profile headline draft:** Find lead-source labels that disappear before reaching the CRM.

**Show, rather than claim:** Twenty synthetic/source rows reconcile campaign labels to CRM fields. Label all examples fictional. Show actual observed test results only after running them. Keep one relevant annotated screenshot or a 45–90 second demo and a one-page scope; no new website, logo, CRM or subscription is required.

**One-call-to-action draft:** “Send a redacted example of the current problem and the result you need. I will confirm whether it fits this fixed scope before proposing paid work.” This is draft copy, not a message sent.

**Response draft for an invited, eligible buyer request:** “Your request mentions [their exact failure]. My proposed deliverable is: find lead-source labels that disappear before reaching the crm. The check I would use is: twenty synthetic/source rows reconcile campaign labels to crm fields. I would first verify whether your existing tools can do this natively. The bounded scope excludes [the project exclusions below]. Are you able to share a redacted example and name the person who will accept the result? I would confirm scope, access and a fixed quote before starting.” Remove any implication of prior client results; do not claim unearned certification.

### $0-first acquisition experiment
Respond only to relevant, current invited implementation requests or a genuine opt-in referral; use one approved professional profile post as secondary discovery.

**Specific discovery phrase:** `UTM form CRM source field missing`. Check current date, location restrictions, budget, exact deliverable, reputation/credential requirements and whether hiring is still open. Search results and community categories are lead-discovery starting points, not a vetted live prospect list.

Prepare at most eight high-fit request records in two batches of four. Obtain owner approval before responses or public posts. Use one reusable proof and personalize the problem, not a generic AI pitch. Stop at four unpaid owner-hours, eight eligible attempts or fourteen elapsed calendar days—whichever comes first—and review what happened. A time-box is not a promised time to first revenue. Pause earlier when no eligible request exists; do not purchase exposure merely to fill a quota.

**Secondary channel:** one relevant, permitted public demonstration or a genuine opt-in referral. No unsolicited mass DMs, scraped email lists or automated applications. Upwork is optional only after eligibility and actual Connects costs are checked; its proposal expense is not assumed zero. Do not move marketplace-sourced pre-contract communication or payment off-platform contrary to its rules.

### Funnel, decision and sale
Record source, eligible request, authorized response, meaningful reply, scoped conversation, funded agreement, accepted delivery, collected receipt, refund and total owner time. Count unpaid likes, followers, waitlist entries and quotes separately from customers. With no meaningful replies after the first four qualified attempts, revise one of buyer/offer/proof before using the second batch; do not simply increase posting volume. With replies but no scoped agreement, record the objection. With no paid commitment at the cap, pause this offer instead of building more features. These are spending/workload gates, not statistical proof of market failure.

Do not begin client-specific production work until there is an agreed scope, lawful permissions, a funded milestone or approved payment arrangement and acceptance criteria. A small paid diagnosis can precede a repair; do not relabel free discovery as a paid deliverable. Ask for a case study or referral only after a real successful delivery and permission.

**Project-specific rejection:** No cross-device identity tracking, consent bypass or claim of incremental ROAS.

### Advertising decision
**Current ad allocation: CAD0.** This narrow service needs proof and qualified conversations before broad paid traffic. Advertised job budgets do not establish conversion economics. Only reassess ads after actual profitable sales; any later test must have a measured conversion path, a conservative acquisition-cost ceiling and a separate approved total budget. No retargeting pixels, uploaded customer lists or campaign launch is authorized by this plan.

**Launch gate:** `buyer_test_only`. For skill-gated work, produce a convincing disposable-environment acceptance test before offering the service. ## Decision and evidence
**Classification:** standalone_service. **Priority:** P3. **Commercial state:** unvalidated. A separately commissioned deliverable is plausible, but it is one offer within a service business, not proof of an independent market.

The sources establish adjacent work or platform capabilities, not a verified exact-scope buyer for this entry. Validate the particular problem before offering or building it. Priority is editorial sequencing for fast, low-upfront-cost experimentation, not probability of success. No workflow implementation, client interview, proposal, contract, paid order or production test was performed for this candidate in this package.

## Buyer, trigger and reason to pay
**Buyer:** Sales + marketing director comparing leads with closed deals.

**Problem/outcome:** Consistent cohort join and explicit unmatched records.

**Buying trigger:** A specific lead ID or source field fails to survive the existing path, preventing reliable operational reporting.

A defensible fee is for resolving the buyer’s specific mapping/operating problem, measured acceptance, failure handling and usable handover—not for owning a template or merely using AI. Ask for one real failure example and the operational consequence. If native configuration or vendor support solves it adequately, use that cheaper route or decline the custom build.

**Native/free/AI alternatives:** Native CRM attribution, ad-platform diagnostics and spreadsheet validation should be checked first.

## Bounded deliverable
Join campaign lead IDs to CRM conversion IDs; produce one audited reconciliation report.

**Pilot cap:** Two authorized exports, explicit join keys and reconciliation totals.

Include a versioned field/rule map, sanitized export where permitted, test results, known limitations, rollback/recovery instructions and customer-owned handover. Changes outside the cap need a new estimate. No external publication, unsolicited messaging, payments/refunds, destructive data changes or account-wide permissions are implied.

## Acceptance and implementation sequence
1. Confirm the current behavior, ownership, destination semantics and one named acceptance decision-maker. Use synthetic/redacted fixtures before requesting production access.
2. Specify the smallest deterministic implementation. Introduce AI only when text variability justifies it; keep a review/abstention path and budget approval.
3. Duplicates, lag and missing IDs do not inflate reported conversion rate.
4. **Distinct failure test:** Unmatched and many-to-many records remain visible; matched revenue is not proof that ads caused the sale.
5. Verify outputs independently of a tool’s “success” response. Test permission loss, retries and partial failures relevant to this scope. Record observed results, residual limitations and restore instructions.
6. Obtain customer acceptance and hand over/revoke temporary access. Do not mark a mock test as a production pass.

**Required access/environment:** Read-only reports with allowed identifiers, an agreed attribution definition and internal alerts only. Production belongs in an appropriately authorized customer-owned account and reliable hosting, not a dependency on the owner’s laptop staying awake. For n8n use cases, check P02 before offering hosted/external configuration access.

## Economics and remaining human work
**New customer-price hypothesis:** CAD350–650 for the stated cap; this is not the owner's startup cost, an observed sale or a conversion of earlier USD ideas. The `historical_price_usd_hypothesis` field, where present, preserves the prior unvalidated USD idea; it is not the current quote. Customer willingness to pay this CAD quote is unverified.

**Efficiency change:** Use permitted exports and a local join; no data warehouse or new subscription.

**Time boundaries:** stop unpaid preparation/qualification for this experiment at four owner-hours total, including the proof; do not build eight custom demos for eight requests. Aim for at most a 60–90 minute reusable fictional proof. The proposed paid delivery allowance is at most 7 hours, including testing and handover, followed by 30–60 minutes of defined defect triage. These are workload limits to validate, not promises that unfamiliar integration work fits them. Quote separately or decline before accepting work that does not fit. Do not omit necessary testing to stay inside the cap.

| Scenario, not forecast | Receipt | Fees / refund reserve assumptions | Allocated cash | All owner hours | Contribution before owner labor/tax | Effective hourly contribution |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Favorable direct at lower quote | CAD350 | 5% combined processing, 0% refund reserve | CAD0 | 9.5 | CAD332.50 | CAD35.00 |
| Marketplace stress at lower quote | CAD350 | 20% fee, 5% refund reserve | CAD25 | 12.5 | CAD237.50 | CAD19.00 |

The favorable scenario allocates one proof hour, one acquisition hour and half an hour of support on top of the delivery cap. The stress case allocates 1.5 proof hours, three acquisition hours and one support hour. Include previous failed pitches and shared business-development time in actual results; they can exceed both examples. The fee percentages are sensitivity assumptions, not assertions of any provider's exact rate. A 20% marketplace case is deliberately conservative; verify the actual provider and contract.

At an illustrative CAD30/hour owner-time target, the stress scenario needs about **CAD533.33** in customer price to break even economically. This is a rejection test, not permission to claim a buyer will pay that price. If that floor exceeds the credible quote, narrow the deliverable without weakening acceptance, use a less costly acquisition channel, or decline. Zero customers produces zero receipts and loses the time/cash spent.

**Unavoidable human work:** qualification, proof of skill, access decisions, scope agreement, ambiguous exceptions, independent acceptance, handover, support and payment reconciliation. Do not call the offer passive. Full methodology: [economics](../../../../../../research/ECONOMICS_V2.md).

## Customer acquisition and validation gate
### Buyer and buying trigger
A marketing operator with existing tools and approved content who needs technical reliability, not guaranteed conversions. A request must actually match **reconcile one campaign export with one sales export using explicit keys**; broad interest in AI is not enough.

### Positioning and proof
**Landing/profile headline draft:** Reconcile one campaign export with one sales export using explicit keys.

**Show, rather than claim:** A matched/unmatched table includes duplicate keys and declared attribution gaps. Label all examples fictional. Show actual observed test results only after running them. Keep one relevant annotated screenshot or a 45–90 second demo and a one-page scope; no new website, logo, CRM or subscription is required.

**One-call-to-action draft:** “Send a redacted example of the current problem and the result you need. I will confirm whether it fits this fixed scope before proposing paid work.” This is draft copy, not a message sent.

**Response draft for an invited, eligible buyer request:** “Your request mentions [their exact failure]. My proposed deliverable is: reconcile one campaign export with one sales export using explicit keys. The check I would use is: a matched/unmatched table includes duplicate keys and declared attribution gaps. I would first verify whether your existing tools can do this natively. The bounded scope excludes [the project exclusions below]. Are you able to share a redacted example and name the person who will accept the result? I would confirm scope, access and a fixed quote before starting.” Remove any implication of prior client results; do not claim unearned certification.

### $0-first acquisition experiment
Respond only to relevant, current invited implementation requests or a genuine opt-in referral; use one approved professional profile post as secondary discovery.

**Specific discovery phrase:** `campaign sales CSV reconciliation report`. Check current date, location restrictions, budget, exact deliverable, reputation/credential requirements and whether hiring is still open. Search results and community categories are lead-discovery starting points, not a vetted live prospect list.

Prepare at most eight high-fit request records in two batches of four. Obtain owner approval before responses or public posts. Use one reusable proof and personalize the problem, not a generic AI pitch. Stop at four unpaid owner-hours, eight eligible attempts or fourteen elapsed calendar days—whichever comes first—and review what happened. A time-box is not a promised time to first revenue. Pause earlier when no eligible request exists; do not purchase exposure merely to fill a quota.

**Secondary channel:** one relevant, permitted public demonstration or a genuine opt-in referral. No unsolicited mass DMs, scraped email lists or automated applications. Upwork is optional only after eligibility and actual Connects costs are checked; its proposal expense is not assumed zero. Do not move marketplace-sourced pre-contract communication or payment off-platform contrary to its rules.

### Funnel, decision and sale
Record source, eligible request, authorized response, meaningful reply, scoped conversation, funded agreement, accepted delivery, collected receipt, refund and total owner time. Count unpaid likes, followers, waitlist entries and quotes separately from customers. With no meaningful replies after the first four qualified attempts, revise one of buyer/offer/proof before using the second batch; do not simply increase posting volume. With replies but no scoped agreement, record the objection. With no paid commitment at the cap, pause this offer instead of building more features. # AWA-092 — Idempotency retrofit service

## Decision and evidence
**Classification:** bundled_component. **Priority:** BUNDLE. **Commercial state:** unvalidated. This is deliberately not counted as a separate launch. Its function can be valuable while its standalone commercial case remains weak.

## Buyer, trigger and reason to pay
**Buyer:** Agency whose workflows double-create objects after retries.

**Problem/outcome:** One event creates no more than one intended object.

**Buying trigger:** An owner needs a reproducible risk/cost finding for a particular workflow, not another generic dashboard.

A defensible fee is for resolving the buyer’s specific mapping/operating problem, measured acceptance, failure handling and usable handover—not for owning a template or merely using AI. Ask for one real failure example and the operational consequence. If native configuration or vendor support solves it adequately, use that cheaper route or decline the custom build.

**Native/free/AI alternatives:** Native retries, logs, vendor support and configuration reviews are often sufficient.

## Bounded deliverable
Introduce stable event ID and duplicate guard; add protected retry semantics.

**Pilot cap:** One side-effecting step, stable event IDs and a durable deduplication design.

Include a versioned field/rule map, sanitized export where permitted, test results, known limitations, rollback/recovery instructions and customer-owned handover. Changes outside the cap need a new estimate. No external publication, unsolicited messaging, payments/refunds, destructive data changes or account-wide permissions are implied.

## Acceptance and implementation sequence
1. Confirm the current behavior, ownership, destination semantics and one named acceptance decision-maker. Use synthetic/redacted fixtures before requesting production access.
2. Specify the smallest deterministic implementation. Introduce AI only when text variability justifies it; keep a review/abstention path and budget approval.
3. 100 duplicate/reordered synthetic events produce one output each.
4. **Distinct failure test:** Concurrent duplicates and a crash between remote success/local acknowledgement are tested; document unresolved ambiguity.
5. Verify outputs independently of a tool’s “success” response. Test permission loss, retries and partial failures relevant to this scope. Record observed results, residual limitations and restore instructions.
6. Obtain customer acceptance and hand over/revoke temporary access. Do not mark a mock test as a production pass.

**Required access/environment:** One redacted workflow export and run sample, with any active testing limited to explicit staging scope. # AWA-095 — Automation cost-cap audit

## Decision and evidence
**Classification:** standalone_service. **Priority:** P2. **Commercial state:** unvalidated. A separately commissioned deliverable is plausible, but it is one offer within a service business, not proof of an independent market.

The sources establish adjacent work or platform capabilities, not a verified exact-scope buyer for this entry. Validate the particular problem before offering or building it. Priority is editorial sequencing for fast, low-upfront-cost experimentation, not probability of success. No workflow implementation, client interview, proposal, contract, paid order or production test was performed for this candidate in this package.

## Buyer, trigger and reason to pay
**Buyer:** Client surprised by excessive per-run credits.

**Problem/outcome:** Credible estimated monthly usage range and cost reducers.

**Buying trigger:** An owner needs a reproducible risk/cost finding for a particular workflow, not another generic dashboard.

A defensible fee is for resolving the buyer’s specific mapping/operating problem, measured acceptance, failure handling and usable handover—not for owning a template or merely using AI. Ask for one real failure example and the operational consequence. If native configuration or vendor support solves it adequately, use that cheaper route or decline the custom build.

**Native/free/AI alternatives:** Native retries, logs, vendor support and configuration reviews are often sufficient.

## Bounded deliverable
Analyze sample execution history and plan limits; model polling and branching cost.

**Pilot cap:** One platform bill/sample, one workflow and three volume scenarios.

Include a versioned field/rule map, sanitized export where permitted, test results, known limitations, rollback/recovery instructions and customer-owned handover. Changes outside the cap need a new estimate. No external publication, unsolicited messaging, payments/refunds, destructive data changes or account-wide permissions are implied.

## Acceptance and implementation sequence
1. Confirm the current behavior, ownership, destination semantics and one named acceptance decision-maker. Use synthetic/redacted fixtures before requesting production access.
2. Specify the smallest deterministic implementation. Introduce AI only when text variability justifies it; keep a review/abstention path and budget approval.
3. Estimate compares with actual sample and flags token-dependent unknowns.
4. **Distinct failure test:** Include polling, filters, branching, retries and external API costs; show which numbers are measured versus assumed.
5. Verify outputs independently of a tool’s “success” response. Test permission loss, retries and partial failures relevant to this scope. Record observed results, residual limitations and restore instructions.
6. Obtain customer acceptance and hand over/revoke temporary access. Do not mark a mock test as a production pass.

**Required access/environment:** One redacted workflow export and run sample, with any active testing limited to explicit staging scope. Production belongs in an appropriately authorized customer-owned account and reliable hosting, not a dependency on the owner’s laptop staying awake. For n8n use cases, check P02 before offering hosted/external configuration access.

## Economics and remaining human work
**New customer-price hypothesis:** CAD220–400 for the stated cap; this is not the owner's startup cost, an observed sale or a conversion of earlier USD ideas. The `historical_price_usd_hypothesis` field, where present, preserves the prior unvalidated USD idea; it is not the current quote. Customer willingness to pay this CAD quote is unverified.

**Efficiency change:** Measure retries, polling and branches; prefer fixing waste over migration.

**Time boundaries:** stop unpaid preparation/qualification for this experiment at four owner-hours total, including the proof; do not build eight custom demos for eight requests. Aim for at most a 60–90 minute reusable fictional proof. The proposed paid delivery allowance is at most 4 hours, including testing and handover, followed by 30–60 minutes of defined defect triage. These are workload limits to validate, not promises that unfamiliar integration work fits them. Quote separately or decline before accepting work that does not fit. Do not omit necessary testing to stay inside the cap.

| Scenario, not forecast | Receipt | Fees / refund reserve assumptions | Allocated cash | All owner hours | Contribution before owner labor/tax | Effective hourly contribution |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Favorable direct at lower quote | CAD220 | 5% combined processing, 0% refund reserve | CAD0 | 6.5 | CAD209.00 | CAD32.15 |
| Marketplace stress at lower quote | CAD220 | 20% fee, 5% refund reserve | CAD25 | 9.5 | CAD140.00 | CAD14.74 |

The favorable scenario allocates one proof hour, one acquisition hour and half an hour of support on top of the delivery cap. The stress case allocates 1.5 proof hours, three acquisition hours and one support hour. Include previous failed pitches and shared business-development time in actual results; they can exceed both examples. The fee percentages are sensitivity assumptions, not assertions of any provider's exact rate. A 20% marketplace case is deliberately conservative; verify the actual provider and contract.

At an illustrative CAD30/hour owner-time target, the stress scenario needs about **CAD413.33** in customer price to break even economically. This is a rejection test, not permission to claim a buyer will pay that price. If that floor exceeds the credible quote, narrow the deliverable without weakening acceptance, use a less costly acquisition channel, or decline. Zero customers produces zero receipts and loses the time/cash spent.

**Unavoidable human work:** qualification, proof of skill, access decisions, scope agreement, ambiguous exceptions, independent acceptance, handover, support and payment reconciliation. Do not call the offer passive. Full methodology: [economics](../../../../../../research/ECONOMICS_V2.md).

## Customer acquisition and validation gate
### Buyer and buying trigger
An agency with an actual client, permitted test data and a named delivery owner. A request must actually match **explain which steps are consuming automation credits before changing plans**; broad interest in AI is not enough.

### Positioning and proof
**Landing/profile headline draft:** Explain which steps are consuming automation credits before changing plans.

**Show, rather than claim:** Three volume scenarios reconcile to an observed redacted bill/run sample. Label all examples fictional. Show actual observed test results only after running them. Keep one relevant annotated screenshot or a 45–90 second demo and a one-page scope; no new website, logo, CRM or subscription is required.

**One-call-to-action draft:** “Send a redacted example of the current problem and the result you need. I will confirm whether it fits this fixed scope before proposing paid work.” This is draft copy, not a message sent.

**Response draft for an invited, eligible buyer request:** “Your request mentions [their exact failure]. My proposed deliverable is: explain which steps are consuming automation credits before changing plans. The check I would use is: three volume scenarios reconcile to an observed redacted bill/run sample. I would first verify whether your existing tools can do this natively. The bounded scope excludes [the project exclusions below]. Are you able to share a redacted example and name the person who will accept the result? I would confirm scope, access and a fixed quote before starting.” Remove any implication of prior client results; do not claim unearned certification.

Manually inspect the official Make Hire Help and n8n Jobs hiring areas for an explicit, eligible request; do not treat For Hire posts as buyers. Use a warm introduction only where genuine.

**Specific discovery phrase:** `Make credits Zapier task usage audit`. Search results and community categories are lead-discovery starting points, not a vetted live prospect list.

Prepare at most eight high-fit request records in two batches of four. Obtain owner approval before responses or public posts. Use one reusable proof and personalize the problem, not a generic AI pitch. Stop at four unpaid owner-hours, eight eligible attempts or fourteen elapsed calendar days—whichever comes first—and review what happened. A time-box is not a promised time to first revenue. Pause earlier when no eligible request exists; do not purchase exposure merely to fill a quota.

**Secondary channel:** one relevant, permitted public demonstration or a genuine opt-in referral. No unsolicited mass DMs, scraped email lists or automated applications. Upwork is optional only after eligibility and actual Connects costs are checked; its proposal expense is not assumed zero. Do not move marketplace-sourced pre-contract communication or payment off-platform contrary to its rules.

### Funnel, decision and sale
Record source, eligible request, authorized response, meaningful reply, scoped conversation, funded agreement, accepted delivery, collected receipt, refund and total owner time. Count unpaid likes, followers, waitlist entries and quotes separately from customers. With no meaningful replies after the first four qualified attempts, revise one of buyer/offer/proof before using the second batch; do not simply increase posting volume. ### Advertising decision
**Current ad allocation: CAD0.** This narrow service needs proof and qualified conversations before broad paid traffic. Advertised job budgets do not establish conversion economics. Only reassess ads after actual profitable sales; any later test must have a measured conversion path, a conservative acquisition-cost ceiling and a separate approved total budget. # AWA-097 — Zapier-to-Make feasibility report

## Decision and evidence
**Classification:** standalone_service. **Priority:** P2. **Commercial state:** unvalidated. A separately commissioned deliverable is plausible, but it is one offer within a service business, not proof of an independent market.

The sources establish adjacent work or platform capabilities, not a verified exact-scope buyer for this entry. Validate the particular problem before offering or building it. Priority is editorial sequencing for fast, low-upfront-cost experimentation, not probability of success. No workflow implementation, client interview, proposal, contract, paid order or production test was performed for this candidate in this package.

## Buyer, trigger and reason to pay
**Buyer:** Business with multi-step Zap and increasing monthly task count.

**Problem/outcome:** Cost and functional parity comparison before any migration.

**Buying trigger:** A buyer has a specific unsupported feature or substantiated cost problem in one established workflow.

A defensible fee is for resolving the buyer’s specific mapping/operating problem, measured acceptance, failure handling and usable handover—not for owning a template or merely using AI. Ask for one real failure example and the operational consequence. If native configuration or vendor support solves it adequately, use that cheaper route or decline the custom build.

**Native/free/AI alternatives:** Stay on the existing platform unless the total migration/maintenance cost is less than the identified limitation.

## Bounded deliverable
Inventory one Zap, map triggers/actions, estimate Make credits and exception handling gaps.

**Pilot cap:** One Zap with at most 5 actions; assessment only before rebuild.

Include a versioned field/rule map, sanitized export where permitted, test results, known limitations, rollback/recovery instructions and customer-owned handover. Changes outside the cap need a new estimate. No external publication, unsolicited messaging, payments/refunds, destructive data changes or account-wide permissions are implied.

## Acceptance and implementation sequence
1. Confirm the current behavior, ownership, destination semantics and one named acceptance decision-maker. Use synthetic/redacted fixtures before requesting production access.
2. Specify the smallest deterministic implementation. Introduce AI only when text variability justifies it; keep a review/abstention path and budget approval.
3. Functional matrix lists unsupported features, price scenarios and rollback option.
4. **Distinct failure test:** Compare polling latency, task/credit counting, connector coverage and support cost; return no-go when savings do not repay migration.
5. Verify outputs independently of a tool’s “success” response. Test permission loss, retries and partial failures relevant to this scope. Record observed results, residual limitations and restore instructions.
6. Obtain customer acceptance and hand over/revoke temporary access. Do not mark a mock test as a production pass.

**Required access/environment:** Sanitized exports, current usage/billing figures, customer-owned target staging and an owner-approved cutover window. Production belongs in an appropriately authorized customer-owned account and reliable hosting, not a dependency on the owner’s laptop staying awake. For n8n use cases, check P02 before offering hosted/external configuration access.

## Economics and remaining human work
**New customer-price hypothesis:** CAD220–400 for the stated cap; this is not the owner's startup cost, an observed sale or a conversion of earlier USD ideas. The `historical_price_usd_hypothesis` field, where present, preserves the prior unvalidated USD idea; it is not the current quote. Customer willingness to pay this CAD quote is unverified.

**Efficiency change:** Use a paper/synthetic feasibility test before building both systems.

**Time boundaries:** stop unpaid preparation/qualification for this experiment at four owner-hours total, including the proof; do not build eight custom demos for eight requests. Aim for at most a 60–90 minute reusable fictional proof. The proposed paid delivery allowance is at most 4 hours, including testing and handover, followed by 30–60 minutes of defined defect triage. These are workload limits to validate, not promises that unfamiliar integration work fits them. Quote separately or decline before accepting work that does not fit. Do not omit necessary testing to stay inside the cap.

| Scenario, not forecast | Receipt | Fees / refund reserve assumptions | Allocated cash | All owner hours | Contribution before owner labor/tax | Effective hourly contribution |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Favorable direct at lower quote | CAD220 | 5% combined processing, 0% refund reserve | CAD0 | 6.5 | CAD209.00 | CAD32.15 |
| Marketplace stress at lower quote | CAD220 | 20% fee, 5% refund reserve | CAD25 | 9.5 | CAD140.00 | CAD14.74 |

The favorable scenario allocates one proof hour, one acquisition hour and half an hour of support on top of the delivery cap. The stress case allocates 1.5 proof hours, three acquisition hours and one support hour. Include previous failed pitches and shared business-development time in actual results; they can exceed both examples. **One-call-to-action draft:** “Send a redacted example of the current problem and the result you need. I will confirm whether it fits this fixed scope before proposing paid work.” This is draft copy, not a message sent.

**Response draft for an invited, eligible buyer request:** “Your request mentions [their exact failure]. My proposed deliverable is: decide whether one zap should move to make at all. The check I would use is: a five-action dependency/feature table compares total switching and run costs. I would first verify whether your existing tools can do this natively. I would confirm scope, access and a fixed quote before starting.” Remove any implication of prior client results; do not claim unearned certification.

### $0-first acquisition experiment
Use explicit spreadsheet/workflow implementation requests and opt-in agency referrals. Prepare a short local proof before considering any paid marketplace proposal.

**Specific discovery phrase:** `Zapier Make migration feasibility cost`. Check current date, location restrictions, budget, exact deliverable, reputation/credential requirements and whether hiring is still open. Search results and community categories are lead-discovery starting points, not a vetted live prospect list.

Prepare at most eight high-fit request records in two batches of four. Obtain owner approval before responses or public posts. A small paid diagnosis can precede a repair; do not relabel free discovery as a paid deliverable. Ask for a case study or referral only after a real successful delivery and permission.

**Project-specific rejection:** Do not recommend moving just because one advertised plan price is lower.

### Advertising decision
**Current ad allocation: CAD0.** This narrow service needs proof and qualified conversations before broad paid traffic. Advertised job budgets do not establish conversion economics. Only reassess ads after actual profitable sales; any later test must have a measured conversion path, a conservative acquisition-cost ceiling and a separate approved total budget. No retargeting pixels, uploaded customer lists or campaign launch is authorized by this plan.

**Launch gate:** `buyer_test_only`. For skill-gated work, produce a convincing disposable-environment acceptance test before offering the service. # AWA-099 — Legacy webhook endpoint cutover

## Decision and evidence
**Classification:** standalone_service. **Priority:** P3. **Commercial state:** unvalidated. A separately commissioned deliverable is plausible, but it is one offer within a service business, not proof of an independent market.

The sources establish adjacent work or platform capabilities, not a verified exact-scope buyer for this entry. Validate the particular problem before offering or building it. Priority is editorial sequencing for fast, low-upfront-cost experimentation, not probability of success. No workflow implementation, client interview, proposal, contract, paid order or production test was performed for this candidate in this package.

## Buyer, trigger and reason to pay
**Buyer:** SMB moving a webhook to a new integration without duplicate events.

**Problem/outcome:** Controlled, reversible endpoint switch for one source.

**Buying trigger:** A buyer has a specific unsupported feature or substantiated cost problem in one established workflow.

A defensible fee is for resolving the buyer’s specific mapping/operating problem, measured acceptance, failure handling and usable handover—not for owning a template or merely using AI. Ask for one real failure example and the operational consequence. If native configuration or vendor support solves it adequately, use that cheaper route or decline the custom build.

**Native/free/AI alternatives:** Stay on the existing platform unless the total migration/maintenance cost is less than the identified limitation.

## Bounded deliverable
Create parallel sandbox handler; test signatures, event IDs and replay; schedule cutover with owner.

**Pilot cap:** One endpoint and event type; controlled owner-approved cutover.

Include a versioned field/rule map, sanitized export where permitted, test results, known limitations, rollback/recovery instructions and customer-owned handover. Changes outside the cap need a new estimate. No external publication, unsolicited messaging, payments/refunds, destructive data changes or account-wide permissions are implied.

## Acceptance and implementation sequence
1. Confirm the current behavior, ownership, destination semantics and one named acceptance decision-maker. Use synthetic/redacted fixtures before requesting production access.
2. Specify the smallest deterministic implementation. Introduce AI only when text variability justifies it; keep a review/abstention path and budget approval.
3. Old/new endpoint comparison includes lost/duplicate checks and rollback rehearsal.
4. **Distinct failure test:** Dual delivery must not duplicate effects; rollback preserves event IDs and records uncertain deliveries for reconciliation.
5. Verify outputs independently of a tool’s “success” response. Test permission loss, retries and partial failures relevant to this scope. Record observed results, residual limitations and restore instructions.
6. Obtain customer acceptance and hand over/revoke temporary access. Do not mark a mock test as a production pass.

**Required access/environment:** Sanitized exports, current usage/billing figures, customer-owned target staging and an owner-approved cutover window. Production belongs in an appropriately authorized customer-owned account and reliable hosting, not a dependency on the owner’s laptop staying awake. For n8n use cases, check P02 before offering hosted/external configuration access.

## Economics and remaining human work
**New customer-price hypothesis:** CAD450–800 for the stated cap; this is not the owner's startup cost, an observed sale or a conversion of earlier USD ideas. The `historical_price_usd_hypothesis` field, where present, preserves the prior unvalidated USD idea; it is not the current quote. Customer willingness to pay this CAD quote is unverified.

**Efficiency change:** Keep the payload contract unchanged; stage the replacement before cutover.

**Time boundaries:** stop unpaid preparation/qualification for this experiment at four owner-hours total, including the proof; do not build eight custom demos for eight requests. Aim for at most a 60–90 minute reusable fictional proof. The proposed paid delivery allowance is at most 8 hours, including testing and handover, followed by 30–60 minutes of defined defect triage. These are workload limits to validate, not promises that unfamiliar integration work fits them. Quote separately or decline before accepting work that does not fit. Do not omit necessary testing to stay inside the cap.

| Scenario, not forecast | Receipt | Fees / refund reserve assumptions | Allocated cash | All owner hours | Contribution before owner labor/tax | Effective hourly contribution |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Favorable direct at lower quote | CAD450 | 5% combined processing, 0% refund reserve | CAD0 | 10.5 | CAD427.50 | CAD40.71 |
| Marketplace stress at lower quote | CAD450 | 20% fee, 5% refund reserve | CAD25 | 13.5 | CAD312.50 | CAD23.15 |

The favorable scenario allocates one proof hour, one acquisition hour and half an hour of support on top of the delivery cap. The stress case allocates 1.5 proof hours, three acquisition hours and one support hour. Include previous failed pitches and shared business-development time in actual results; they can exceed both examples. The fee percentages are sensitivity assumptions, not assertions of any provider's exact rate. A 20% marketplace case is deliberately conservative; verify the actual provider and contract.

At an illustrative CAD30/hour owner-time target, the stress scenario needs about **CAD573.33** in customer price to break even economically. This is a rejection test, not permission to claim a buyer will pay that price. If that floor exceeds the credible quote, narrow the deliverable without weakening acceptance, use a less costly acquisition channel, or decline. Zero customers produces zero receipts and loses the time/cash spent.

**Unavoidable human work:** qualification, proof of skill, access decisions, scope agreement, ambiguous exceptions, independent acceptance, handover, support and payment reconciliation. Do not call the offer passive. Full methodology: [economics](../../../../../../research/ECONOMICS_V2.md).

### Buyer and buying trigger
An agency with an actual client, permitted test data and a named delivery owner. A request must actually match **change one webhook endpoint with a checked rollback and replay plan**; broad interest in AI is not enough.

### Positioning and proof
**Landing/profile headline draft:** Change one webhook endpoint with a checked rollback and replay plan.

**Show, rather than claim:** Old/new endpoints receive synthetic events once, with cutover and rollback evidence. Label all examples fictional. Show actual observed test results only after running them. Keep one relevant annotated screenshot or a 45–90 second demo and a one-page scope; no new website, logo, CRM or subscription is required.

**One-call-to-action draft:** “Send a redacted example of the current problem and the result you need. I will confirm whether it fits this fixed scope before proposing paid work.” This is draft copy, not a message sent.

**Response draft for an invited, eligible buyer request:** “Your request mentions [their exact failure]. My proposed deliverable is: change one webhook endpoint with a checked rollback and replay plan. The check I would use is: old/new endpoints receive synthetic events once, with cutover and rollback evidence. I would first verify whether your existing tools can do this natively. The bounded scope excludes [the project exclusions below]. Are you able to share a redacted example and name the person who will accept the result? I would confirm scope, access and a fixed quote before starting.” Remove any implication of prior client results; do not claim unearned certification.

### $0-first acquisition experiment
Manually inspect the official Make Hire Help and n8n Jobs hiring areas for an explicit, eligible request; do not treat For Hire posts as buyers. Use a warm introduction only where genuine.

**Specific discovery phrase:** `webhook endpoint migration cutover rollback`. Check current date, location restrictions, budget, exact deliverable, reputation/credential requirements and whether hiring is still open. Search results and community categories are lead-discovery starting points, not a vetted live prospect list.

Prepare at most eight high-fit request records in two batches of four. Obtain owner approval before responses or public posts. Use one reusable proof and personalize the problem, not a generic AI pitch. Stop at four unpaid owner-hours, eight eligible attempts or fourteen elapsed calendar days—whichever comes first—and review what happened. A time-box is not a promised time to first revenue. Pause earlier when no eligible request exists; do not purchase exposure merely to fill a quota.

**Secondary channel:** one relevant, permitted public demonstration or a genuine opt-in referral. No unsolicited mass DMs, scraped email lists or automated applications. Upwork is optional only after eligibility and actual Connects costs are checked; its proposal expense is not assumed zero. Do not move marketplace-sourced pre-contract communication or payment off-platform contrary to its rules.

### Funnel, decision and sale
Record source, eligible request, authorized response, meaningful reply, scoped conversation, funded agreement, accepted delivery, collected receipt, refund and total owner time. Count unpaid likes, followers, waitlist entries and quotes separately from customers. With no meaningful replies after the first four qualified attempts, revise one of buyer/offer/proof before using the second batch; do not simply increase posting volume. With replies but no scoped agreement, record the objection. With no paid commitment at the cap, pause this offer instead of building more features. These are spending/workload gates, not statistical proof of market failure.

Do not begin client-specific production work until there is an agreed scope, lawful permissions, a funded milestone or approved payment arrangement and acceptance criteria. A small paid diagnosis can precede a repair; do not relabel free discovery as a paid deliverable. Ask for a case study or referral only after a real successful delivery and permission.

**Project-specific rejection:** Only sell with demonstrated experience and scheduled owner-controlled deployment access.

### Advertising decision
**Current ad allocation: CAD0.** This narrow service needs proof and qualified conversations before broad paid traffic. Advertised job budgets do not establish conversion economics. Only reassess ads after actual profitable sales; any later test must have a measured conversion path, a conservative acquisition-cost ceiling and a separate approved total budget. No retargeting pixels, uploaded customer lists or campaign launch is authorized by this plan.

**Launch gate:** `skill_gated`. For skill-gated work, produce a convincing disposable-environment acceptance test before offering the service. For follow-ons, do not advertise before the earlier project actually has paying clients.
